<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

You are an autonomous engineer. The repository at /workspace is at an earlier state of a real-world project.

`/workspace/requirements/` contains every requirement as a separate file. Each file describes one change request. Read them all, implement every one. Order does not matter, but some changes depend on others.



You are running as a long-horizon autonomous engineering agent at
`/workspace`. This task spans many files and requirements, and is expected
to take many iterations.

Read every requirement under `/workspace/requirements/` (and any other
explicit requirement list referenced by the task) and only finish once
every single one is addressed. Cherry-picking or partial fixes will lead
to failure.



## Optional planning artifact

If you believe the task is complex enough to benefit from a plan, you may
write `/workspace/agent_plans/plan.json` before making changes. This is
optional. If you create it, it must be a JSON object with `nodes` and
`edges`. Each node must have string `id` equal to a requirement slug from
`/workspace/requirements/`, may include `label` and `layer`, and each edge
must use string `from` and `to` that reference those ids.



## Git workflow (required)

`/workspace` is initialized as a git repo. After finishing the
implementation for ONE requirement:

  1. `cd /workspace`
  2. `git add -A`
  3. `git diff --cached > requirement_patches/<slug>.diff`
  4. `git commit -m "impl: <slug>"`

Where `<slug>` is the requirement filename without the `.yaml` extension.
The patch file MUST be non-empty for the requirement to count as complete.
Never write or `touch` an empty `.diff` file.

You may run `git log`, `git diff`, `git show` at any time to inspect what
prior work has done — only your own commits will be there; no reference
solution is accessible.

## Recommended workflow

1. Read the task carefully and survey `/workspace` so you understand the
   code you are changing.
2. As a development agent, when implementing a requirement you may write
   tests under `/workspace/agent_tests/` to safeguard correctness and
   future stability — write them if you think they help, otherwise skip.
3. Keep iterating until every requirement is implemented. Do not stop at a
   partial fix, a first passing check, or one successful edit.
4. Do not narrow the scope on your own. Missing a requirement is a task
   failure even if the changed tests pass.
5. You may revise the same files and rerun focused checks as many times as
   needed before finishing.
6. Your final summary must report requirement coverage counts, including at
   least the total number of requirements reviewed and how many were
   implemented and blocked.

title: Update version_date.tsv and changelogs after v22.10.1.1875-stable
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse operators and package consumers depend on the published release metadata to know which stable build they are installing and what changed in that release. This shard is a release-packaging update rather than a new runtime feature, but the release artifacts still need to present a complete and accurate `v22.10.1.1875-stable` entry.


  ## Desired outcome

  Refresh the stable release metadata so version manifests, packaged images, and the changelog consistently describe `v22.10.1.1875-stable`. This is release bookkeeping only: the runtime behavior of ClickHouse itself should stay exactly as delivered by the already-selected release contents.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Operators inspecting packaged version data, release notes, or image metadata all see the same stable version identifier and changelog entry for `v22.10.1.1875-stable`, with no unintended behavioral changes beyond the release announcement itself.

  '

title: Implement backup to S3
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator needs to keep table backups in object storage rather than only local destinations, and the backup workflow should work the same way whether the S3 target is written directly in SQL or referenced through a named collection.


  ## Desired outcome

  `BACKUP ... TO S3(''endpoint/path'', ''key'', ''secret'')` and `RESTORE ... FROM S3(''endpoint/path'', ''key'', ''secret'')` should be supported, and the same workflow should also work with `S3(named_collection_s3_backups, ''backup_name'')` so teams can restore from S3 without embedding credentials in every statement.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A table can be backed up to S3 and restored from the same backup location with normal `BACKUP` and `RESTORE` semantics, and environments that can use server-side copying continue to report that native copy is being used.

  '
====
title: Disable zero-copy replication by default
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using replicated storage on shared object storage have been getting zero-copy replication by default even though that path is still risky enough to surprise clusters that did not explicitly choose it.

  ## Desired outcome

  Zero-copy replication should become an opt-in capability so the safer default replication behavior is used unless an operator enables the feature deliberately.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A cluster does not use zero-copy replication unless the relevant configuration is explicitly turned on, and existing deployments no longer inherit it by default.

  '

args.description: Implement 773 ClickHouse requirements in parallel batches
args.prompt_template:
You are one of many autonomous engineering agents working CONCURRENTLY in the ClickHouse repository at /workspace (checked out at an older state, around mid-2022 / v22.6 era). Each file in /workspace/requirements/ is a YAML describing one change request (a generalized description of a real historical ClickHouse change). Other agents are editing and committing in the same repo at the same time — follow the git rules below exactly.

Your assigned requirement slugs (comma-separated):
{{item}}

Process each slug independently, in order:

1. Read /workspace/requirements/<slug>.yaml in full.
2. Locate the relevant code with Grep/Glob/Read. The requirement's Context / Desired outcome / Acceptance signals describe a real change that was made to this codebase — infer the concrete minimal edit (source code, config, docs, tests, CI workflows, build files, etc.). Keep changes minimal, consistent with surrounding style, and scoped to the requirement. Do NOT try to build the whole project (far too slow); at most run quick targeted checks (python scripts, grep-based verification, a fast unit-level compile of a single file if truly needed). Some requirements are release bookkeeping (version_date.tsv, changelogs, SECURITY.md), some are doc/test-only edits, some are small C++ fixes or cleanups — judge from the text.
3. Commit that requirement — and only that requirement — with this exact pattern:
   cd /workspace && flock /tmp/ch_git.lock bash -c 'git add <file1> <file2> ... && mkdir -p requirement_patches && git diff --cached > requirement_patches/<slug>.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: <slug>"'
   Rules:
   - NEVER run `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git add -u`, and never stage files you did not change for THIS requirement.
   - The requirement_patches/<slug>.diff file itself must never be staged or committed.
   - After committing, verify requirement_patches/<slug>.diff is non-empty (use `wc -c`). An empty diff means the requirement does not count as complete. If empty, your change did not alter any tracked file — make a real change and recommit. Never leave an empty .diff file.
   - If the git command fails (lock error, nothing staged, etc.), diagnose and retry.
4. Shared-file safety: if a requirement touches files that many other requirements also touch (e.g. utils/list-versions/version_date.tsv, SECURITY.md, popular docs files, src/Core/Settings.h, CI workflow files), wrap the EDIT plus the stage/diff/commit in ONE flock critical section (script the edit with python3 or sed inside the locked bash -c, then add/diff/commit) so a concurrent agent's half-finished edit to the same file cannot leak into your staged diff. Keep locked sections short.
5. If you see working-tree changes you did not make, leave them alone — never revert, stash, or clean them.
6. Commit each requirement IMMEDIATELY after finishing its edits, before starting the next slug.

If a requirement is genuinely unimplementable as stated, still make the best-faith minimal change matching its intent so a meaningful non-empty diff exists, and note that in your report.

When finished with ALL assigned slugs, reply with a compact per-slug report, one line each: `<slug>: done|blocked — one-line summary`.

title: Add ldapr to AArch64 server builds
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams running ClickHouse on modern AArch64 cloud hardware expect the server builds to take advantage of the architectural features that are commonly available on Graviton2-class and similar instances. Leaving out `ldapr` means heavily contended code paths and allocator workloads can miss performance that newer ARM systems should be able to deliver.


  ## Desired outcome

  Modern AArch64 server binaries are built with `ldapr` enabled alongside the existing ARMv8.2 feature bundle, while non-AArch64 and older compatibility builds continue to follow their current paths. The change is performance-oriented and does not alter SQL behavior or user-facing interfaces.

  '
title: ActionsDAG rename index to outputs
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse developers working on expression planning need internal graph terminology that reflects the current abstraction instead of older indexing language. This rename should improve readability without changing any user-visible query behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  The internal `ActionsDAG` API should use `outputs` terminology consistently in place of the old `index` naming where that concept now represents produced nodes.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected interpreter and planning code compiles against the new terminology, and query results and planner behavior remain unchanged from a user perspective.

  '

payload.output:
title: Correct implementation of AggregateState comparison
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user comparing aggregate states should get correct and stable behavior even when those states involve more complex underlying types such as `Decimal`.


  ## Desired outcome

  Comparisons involving `AggregateState` values should use the proper type handling so rare but valid comparisons do not fail because of an invalid cast in the comparison path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries that compare aggregate states with complex nested types produce the expected result instead of failing on an incorrect cast, and existing aggregate-state comparison behavior stays intact for simpler types.

  '
title: full example using AggregatingMergeTree
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users learning `AggregatingMergeTree` often struggle to turn the individual documentation fragments into a complete working example. The existing docs do not show the full flow clearly enough for someone trying to reproduce it.


  ## Desired outcome

  Provide a fuller end-to-end example that demonstrates how a real `AggregatingMergeTree` workflow is meant to be set up and queried.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The documentation includes a complete example sequence rather than isolated fragments, and a reader can follow it to understand the intended `AggregatingMergeTree` usage pattern.

  '
title: minor fix error msg, replace outdated func name
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When aggregation merge preparation receives no data at all, developers and operators rely on the exception text to identify the failing code path quickly. An outdated method name in that message makes debugging harder because the exception points to the wrong function.


  ## Desired outcome

  The empty-input exception in the aggregator should name `Aggregator::prepareVariantsToMerge` instead of the older `Aggregator::mergeAndConvertToBlocks`, while keeping the same failure condition and error code. This is a diagnostics fix only.


  ## Acceptance signals

  If aggregation merge preparation is invoked with no variants, ClickHouse still throws `EMPTY_DATA_PASSED`, but the message now correctly says `Empty data passed to Aggregator::prepareVariantsToMerge.` so logs and error reports identify the real failing routine.

  '

title: Add some guard rails around aggregation memory management
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  The aggregation function interface allows implementation mistakes around destruction and memory ownership that are easy to miss during development. This is internal hardening in a correctness-sensitive subsystem, so existing query behavior must stay unchanged.


  ## Desired outcome

  Add guard rails that make incorrect aggregation-memory management harder to introduce while preserving the current public aggregate-function contract.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The touched aggregation API enforces the new safety expectation, and existing aggregate-function behavior remains unchanged for users.

  '
title: Analyzer change setting into allow_experimental_analyzer
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator or SQL user who wants to try the new query analyzer needs one clear switch that consistently controls that behavior across query entry points. The current setting name reads like a stable feature toggle even though the analyzer is still experimental, which makes session settings, diagnostics, and rollout guidance harder to understand.


  ## Desired outcome

  The experimental analyzer should be exposed under the setting name `allow_experimental_analyzer`, and that same name should govern analyzer-backed behavior anywhere the feature is consulted, including statements that inspect queries such as `DESCRIBE` and `EXPLAIN`. Users enabling the analyzer should no longer have to rely on the older `use_analyzer` name.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A user who enables `allow_experimental_analyzer` gets analyzer-based behavior in the same places where the old flag was previously checked, and the exposed setting name clearly communicates that the feature is experimental rather than generally enabled by default.

  '
title: Fix formatting of `ALTER FREEZE`
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user relying on formatted SQL output expects maintenance statements to be rendered consistently, especially when inspecting or replaying `ALTER` queries.


  ## Desired outcome

  `ALTER ... FREEZE` statements should be formatted cleanly and consistently by the SQL formatter, without awkward token placement or spacing that makes the statement harder to read.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Formatting an `ALTER FREEZE` query produces stable, human-readable SQL output that matches the style of other `ALTER` statements and does not change the underlying query semantics.

  '
title: Fix `ALTER ADD COLUMN`  with columns of type `Object`
category: bugfix
requirement: 'A user evolving a MergeTree or ReplicatedMergeTree table should be able to add a JSON/Object column with ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN and then keep querying both old and new rows successfully. With allow_experimental_object_type = 1, existing rows should remain readable after the schema change and newly inserted rows should be able to populate the added JSON column normally. The desired outcome is that late-added Object columns behave like a supported schema evolution path instead of breaking reads.

  '

=== amqp-cpp-revision ===
title: Update amqp-cpp
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The bundled `amqp-cpp` dependency needs an update to resolve known issues in the current version without changing the ClickHouse SQL surface.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update `amqp-cpp` to the newer revision required by ClickHouse. This is an internal dependency maintenance task, so the observable AMQP-facing behavior should remain compatible except for the bugfixes delivered by the dependency update.


  ## Acceptance signals

  ClickHouse builds and runs against the newer `amqp-cpp` revision, and the targeted AMQP issue is resolved without introducing new user-facing interface changes.

  '
=== analyzer-aggregate-lambda-rejection ===
title: Analyzer aggregate function lambda crash fix
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user experimenting with the new analyzer can write expressions where lambda syntax is attached to an aggregate or window function. Today that path can reach unresolved function nodes and end in an internal exception instead of a clear user-facing rejection.


  ## Desired outcome

  If a lambda is supplied to a function that does not support lambda arguments, analysis should fail deterministically with a clear exception rather than a logical error or unresolved-node failure. In particular, aggregate and window functions must reject lambda arguments explicitly, and unresolved function nodes should report that the function node with that name is not resolved.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries that misuse lambda arguments on aggregate or window functions raise `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD` with messages such as `Aggregate function ''...'' does not support lambda arguments` or `Window function ''...'' does not support lambda arguments`, instead of crashing in analysis. Other argument-validation messages in the analyzer continue to reference the quoted function name consistently.'
=== analyzer-cte-scope ===
title: Analyzer CTE resolution fix
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts using common table expressions inside nested queries expect each reference to resolve in the correct scope, but the analyzer can currently bind a CTE incorrectly when it appears under a subquery boundary.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix CTE resolution in the analyzer so nested and subquery-local references resolve to the intended `WITH` definition.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries that use CTEs inside subqueries analyze and execute correctly, without unresolved references or accidental binding to the wrong scope.

  '
=== analyzer-join-constants ===
title: Analyzer improve JOIN with constants
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The analyzer has trouble with `JOIN` conditions that include constant expressions alongside the real join predicates. Users can write valid SQL that should be planned correctly but currently gets mishandled.


  ## Desired outcome

  `JOIN` analysis should tolerate constant terms in the `ON` clause without corrupting the join-condition handling or changing the intended semantics.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected `JOIN` forms with constants are analyzed successfully, and constant expressions in the `ON` clause no longer cause the planner to reject or mis-handle otherwise valid queries.

  '
=== analyzer-key-condition-crash ===
title: Analyzer AST key condition crash fix
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The analyzer can fail on a specific AST key-condition pattern that users can reach with valid SQL. Instead of planning the query or rejecting it cleanly, the server hits an internal exception.


  ## Desired outcome

  The analyzer should handle that key-condition form robustly so users can run the query pattern without tripping an internal failure.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The previously failing key-condition query no longer raises the internal exception, and the analyzer produces a normal plan or a regular user-facing error if the query is invalid for some other reason.

  '
=== annoy-index-doc-polish ===
title: Minor fixes in annoy index documentation
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts experimenting with approximate nearest-neighbor search need the Annoy index documentation to describe the feature correctly, because most users discover its limits and syntax from the docs rather than from the source.


  ## Desired outcome

  Tighten the Annoy index documentation so the guidance, terminology, and examples match the actual feature and do not create false expectations about how the index should be configured or used.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reader can use the page as a trustworthy reference for Annoy indexes without running into contradictions, ambiguous wording, or examples that do not reflect real behavior.

  '
=== annoy-index-validation ===
title: Fix bad_cast in Annoy index
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user creating an `Annoy` index needs invalid definitions to be rejected up front with clear guidance instead of running into unstable behavior later during inserts or index use.


  ## Desired outcome

  `Annoy` indexes should only be accepted on a single column of a supported vector type, and unsupported definitions should fail with clear validation, including the message `Annoy indexes must be created on a single column` and type guidance that only `Array(Float32)` and `Tuple(Float32)` are supported.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Invalid `Annoy` index definitions are rejected during setup with readable user-facing exceptions, while valid single-column float-vector indexes continue to build and work normally.

  '

payload.output:
title: Suppress "Cannot find column <subquery> in ActionsDAG result"
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A query planner problem that surfaces as a server-side logical error is confusing for users and can look like an internal failure instead of a normal query mistake.

  ## Desired outcome

  When a projected subquery column cannot be found during `ActionsDAG` merging, ClickHouse should report it as a client-visible identifier problem rather than an internal logical error.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The failure should be classified as `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` instead of `LOGICAL_ERROR`, so the client sees a regular query exception rather than behavior associated with an internal invariant violation.

  '
title: Add constexpr
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  This is internal C++ maintenance in aggregate-function code, and users should not observe any change in aggregate semantics just because compile-time constants are expressed more precisely.


  ## Desired outcome

  Introduce the compile-time cleanup needed here while keeping the runtime behavior, return values, and public aggregate contracts unchanged.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The code builds with the new constant-expression form, and aggregate behavior remains identical from a user''s point of view.

  '
title: Yet another fix for AggregateFunctionMinMaxAny
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts using aggregates derived from `AggregateFunctionMinMaxAny` can get incorrect behavior on empty inputs, especially in cases where `singleValueOrNull` should return a clean empty result instead of leaking an invalid state.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make these aggregate states serialize, merge, and finalize correctly for empty-input cases so `singleValueOrNull` and related behavior remain well-defined.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Empty-input queries return the correct empty or `NULL` result instead of a corrupted value, and the aggregate remains stable across normal execution paths.

  '
title: Fix another bug in AggregateFunctionMinMaxAny
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  An analyst using `singleValueOrNull`, `min`, `max`, or related single-result aggregates expects empty-input behavior to stay consistent instead of silently turning into a non-null value after internal state merges. There is a corner case in `AggregateFunctionMinMaxAny` where an empty state can be mishandled and produce the wrong result after aggregation.


  ## Desired outcome

  When the aggregate input is empty, the result should remain the same nullable empty-state outcome users already expect, even after the function’s internal state is merged or finalized. Empty datasets must not suddenly report a concrete value just because the aggregate passed through a particular implementation path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The existing empty-input reference query gains the missing final `1`, confirming that the aggregate now reports the correct state for that edge case while the earlier `\N` results remain unchanged. Normal non-empty aggregate results are unaffected.'

1	title: Better logging for asynchronous inserts
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A ClickHouse operator may enable asynchronous inserts and still see some `INSERT` statements run synchronously, but today it is difficult to tell from the logs why that fallback happened.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  When `async_insert=1` is set but ClickHouse executes the query synchronously, the debug log should explain the reason in operator terms, including cases where the asynchronous queue is not configured, the `INSERT` reads from `SELECT`, or the query does not contain inlined data.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The execution behavior stays the same, but fallback-to-synchronous cases now leave a specific diagnostic reason in the logs so operators can distinguish configuration problems from unsupported query shapes.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Fix reading from async read buffer with direct io
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When asynchronous readers use direct I/O or remote object-storage backends, seeking to the end of a fetched buffer should behave like a normal boundary condition instead of being treated as an invalid state.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Make asynchronous buffered reads handle the case where the current offset exactly matches the fetched chunk size, so end-of-buffer and EOF transitions are correct and do not expose stale or duplicated bytes.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  Direct-I/O and remote/HDFS asynchronous reads return only the unread portion of a prefetched block, and an exact end-of-buffer seek cleanly reports no remaining bytes instead of misbehaving.
14	
15	  '

1	title: Add documentation for `system.asynchronous_metrics`.
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Operators use `system.asynchronous_metrics` and Prometheus exports to understand background resource usage, but many metrics do not explain themselves and some cache-disk metrics are incomplete. That makes observability harder than it needs to be.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Expose human-meaningful documentation alongside asynchronous metrics and make the relevant cache-disk measurements reflect all applicable disks, not just an arbitrary subset.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The metric documentation is available both from `system.asynchronous_metrics` and in the Prometheus `# HELP` output, and the affected cache-disk metrics aggregate across all cache disks in the server.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Add system table `asynchronous_insert_log`
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Users relying on asynchronous inserts, especially with `wait_for_async_insert=0`, currently have little built-in visibility into what happened after the server accepted the query. That makes it hard to answer basic operational questions such as when a batch flushed, whether it succeeded, and what exception was associated with a failed asynchronous write.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Add a system table named `asynchronous_insert_log` that records the lifecycle of asynchronous inserts, including fire-and-forget submissions. Operators should be able to inspect timing fields such as `event_time_microseconds` and `flush_time_microseconds`, identify the target database and table, and see any captured exception information for failed entries.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  After asynchronous inserts run, users can query `system.asynchronous_insert_log` to understand enqueue, flush, success, and failure behavior without guessing from unrelated logs. The table becomes the standard introspection surface for asynchronous insert diagnostics.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Terminate AsynchronousInsertQueue w/o waiting for timeout
2	category: other
3	requirement: 'Shutting down a server with asynchronous inserts enabled should not stall until the queue’s wake-up timeout expires. `AsynchronousInsertQueue` needs an immediate termination path so process shutdown can wake the queue, stop background work promptly, and exit predictably even when no new inserts arrive to trigger the worker.
4	
5	  '

1	title: Fix annoying messages in AsynchronousMetrics
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When ClickHouse cannot collect some block-device statistics, the asynchronous metrics subsystem emits noisy and unhelpful messages. Operators need a clearer diagnostic that explains what failed without spamming confusing output.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Keep the metrics collection behavior the same, but improve the wording of the surfaced message so it is concise and understandable.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The affected diagnostic is reported as `Cannot read statistics from block devices: ...`, and operators no longer see the previous noisy phrasing for that failure.
16	
17	  '

2	category: other
3	requirement: 'Running `BACKUP` on `MergeTree` tables in an Atomic database should not depend on creating hardlinks that can interfere with concurrent backup and restore activity across replicas. Operators need `BACKUP ... ON CLUSTER ... ASYNC` jobs to finish with `BACKUP_CREATED`, and a later restore should reconstruct the right data on each replica even when multiple cluster backups are happening at once.

payload.output:
title: move title to frontmatter in Backup docs
category: refactor
requirement: 'Backup documentation should expose its page title through frontmatter so it can be reused cleanly by the documentation system without changing the meaning of the page. Readers should see the same backup guidance, but the page metadata needs to support inclusion and rendering in the modern docs pipeline.

  '
title: Improve referential dependencies
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator restoring backups expects dependent objects to come back in a valid order, especially when databases, tables, views, dictionaries, users, roles, settings profiles, and `ON CLUSTER` objects reference one another. Today referential dependencies are incomplete enough that restore order can be wrong, causing restore failures even though the backup itself is valid.


  ## Desired outcome

  Backup restore should build a more complete dependency graph so referenced objects are restored only after the objects they depend on are available. This includes database and table references embedded in DDL, cluster-aware objects, and other named entities such as users, roles, and settings profiles that participate in restore ordering.


  ## Acceptance signals

  End-to-end restore scenarios can create and back up objects such as `test.table`, users like `u1`, roles like `r1` and `r2`, and settings profiles like `prof1`, then drop them and restore them without dependency-order failures. Restores on a cluster also succeed when tables are created and recovered with `ON CLUSTER ''cluster''` or `ON CLUSTER ''cluster3''`, confirming that the dependency graph now captures those referential links.'
title: Implement backup to S3
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator needs to keep table backups in object storage rather than only local destinations, and the backup workflow should work the same way whether the S3 target is written directly in SQL or referenced through a named collection.


  ## Desired outcome

  `BACKUP ... TO S3(''endpoint/path'', ''key'', ''secret'')` and `RESTORE ... FROM S3(''endpoint/path'', ''key'', ''secret'')` should be supported, and the same workflow should also work with `S3(named_collection_s3_backups, ''backup_name'')` so teams can restore from S3 without embedding credentials in every statement.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A table can be backed up to S3 and restored from the same backup location with normal `BACKUP` and `RESTORE` semantics, and environments that can use server-side copying continue to report that native copy is being used.

  '

=== compact-part-marks ===
title: Fix compressed marks read for compact parts
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users running MergeTree tables with compact parts and compressed marks can hit read failures because ClickHouse validates the marks file as if it were uncompressed. That makes a valid part look corrupt after restart or reload even though the stored marks are fine.


  ## Desired outcome

  Compact parts with compressed marks should be read according to the compressed format, and ClickHouse should only use the fixed-size marks-file check for uncompressed marks. If a marks file is genuinely truncated or incomplete, the read path should fail with `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA` and the message `Cannot read all marks from file {}`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Tables that use compact parts with compressed marks can be reopened and queried successfully after restart, while truly incomplete marks files still fail with the explicit `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA` contract. Valid compressed data is no longer mistaken for corruption.

  '
=== compact-part-mutation ===
title: optimize compact part mutation
category: other
requirement: 'Mutations on compact parts should avoid unnecessary work so they finish faster and with less overhead on heavily updated tables. The optimized path must preserve mutation correctness, but operators should see less wasted processing when a compact part can be rewritten more efficiently.

  '
=== compound-expression-crash ===
title: Analyzer compound expression crash fix
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts using the experimental analyzer can hit an exception when a query contains certain compound expressions, turning a normal query-validation problem into an internal failure.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make compound expressions analyze cleanly so those queries either execute normally or fail with an ordinary semantic error instead of triggering an internal exception.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries with the affected compound-expression shape no longer hit an analyzer exception, and the analyzer preserves normal query semantics for valid statements.

  '
=== compression-context-cleanup ===
title: free compression and decompression contexts
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users of the self-extracting ClickHouse binary should be able to compress and decompress archives repeatedly without the helper tool leaking compression resources on success or on early error paths.

  ## Desired outcome

  Ensure the self-extracting compressor and decompressor always release their ZSTD contexts so packaging and extraction runs remain stable over repeated use.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Compression and decompression still succeed as before, but the helper process no longer retains `ZSTD` contexts after either normal completion or failure.

  '
=== concurrent-threads-soft-limit-split ===
title: split concurrent_threads_soft_limit setting into two
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators need a predictable way to limit total query-processing threads across the server without relying on one overloaded setting or a magic value tied to CPU count.

  ## Desired outcome

  ClickHouse should expose two separate server settings, `concurrent_threads_soft_limit_num` and `concurrent_threads_soft_limit_ratio_to_cores`, so administrators can choose an absolute cap, a cap relative to logical cores, or both together.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A value of `0` in either setting must mean that setting is unlimited, the effective limit must be the smaller non-zero cap when both are set, and the old `concurrent_threads_soft_limit` behavior with the `-1` heuristic must no longer be the user-facing contract.

  '
=== config-profile-cleanup ===
title: Remove trash from config
category: refactor
requirement: 'The built-in user configuration should stop carrying legacy profile clutter that is no longer part of the intended defaults, but profile semantics must remain stable for administrators. Existing introspection and assignment behavior through `defaultProfiles()`, `currentProfiles()`, and `enabledProfiles()` should keep making sense, profile changes should still be reflected through `SHOW CREATE` and the relevant system tables, and changing default profiles should continue to affect new sessions rather than silently rewriting the state of already-running connections.

  '
=== configreloader-shutdown-race ===
title: Stop `ConfigReloader` first to avoid data race
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Server shutdown can race with configuration reloading, producing a ThreadSanitizer-reported data race during teardown. Operators need shutdown to be orderly and race-free, especially when diagnosing concurrency issues.


  ## Desired outcome

  Stop configuration reloading early enough in the shutdown sequence that the rest of server teardown cannot race with it.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `ConfigReloader` is stopped before the later server teardown steps begin, and the shutdown path no longer triggers the reported race in this area.

  '

title: Fix locking while writing backup in multiple threads
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users creating backups with multiple worker threads expect direct file-copy paths to benefit from concurrency rather than being serialized behind an unnecessary global lock.


  ## Desired outcome

  Backup writing should only hold the global lock where correctness actually requires it, such as archive writes, while regular multi-threaded file writes and native-copy paths can proceed concurrently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Non-archive backup writes no longer block each other unnecessarily, archive writes remain serialized for correctness, and the file-count bookkeeping stays thread-safe.

  '
title: fix bandwidth throttlers initialization order
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators who configure global network bandwidth limits expect those throttles to apply predictably, but the current initialization order can leave the all-users throttler in the wrong state before per-user throttling is derived from it. That creates confusing traffic-control behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  Initialize bandwidth throttlers in the correct order so global and per-user limits are both built from a valid shared configuration.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `max_network_bandwidth_for_all_users` is established before the dependent user throttlers are created, and the configured network limits behave consistently after startup.

  '
title: Fix reusing of files > 4GB from base backup
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator using incremental backups with `SETTINGS base_backup = ...` expects unchanged files to be reused even when a single column file is larger than 4 GiB.

  ## Desired outcome

  Backups should identify those large files as reusable content instead of duplicating them or treating them as overflowed sizes.

  ## Acceptance signals

  An incremental backup of an unchanged part with a 4 GiB+ data file can be created and restored successfully, and the incremental backup stores only the backup metadata when no data file actually changed.

  '
title: Simplify Base58 encoding/decoding
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse users already rely on the existing Base58 SQL functions when they need compact text representations of binary identifiers, keys, and hashes, and they should not have to care which low-level library is underneath them.

  ## Desired outcome

  Keep Base58 encoding and decoding available with the same user-facing behavior, but make the implementation lighter and easier to maintain so deployments are not tied to an extra bundled dependency for this path.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries that use the Base58 encode/decode functions continue to work without any SQL changes, round trips still preserve the same values, and administrators do not need a separate Base58 third-party component to ship this capability.

  '

title: Add support of Date32 arguments for formatDateTime and FROM_UNIXTIME functions
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts often store calendar values as `Date32` because they need ranges outside the classic `Date` limits, but they still want to format those values with the same helpers used for timestamps. Today `formatDateTime` and `FROM_UNIXTIME` reject `Date32`, forcing awkward casts and making older dates harder to work with.


  ## Desired outcome

  `formatDateTime` and `FROM_UNIXTIME` should accept `Date32` wherever date-like inputs are already supported, while preserving their existing argument-count rules and string-format/timezone arguments. Error reporting should keep naming the offending position clearly, such as referring to the first, second, or third argument, so users know exactly what to fix.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A `Date32` value can be passed to `formatDateTime` and to multi-argument `FROM_UNIXTIME` without an explicit cast, formatted output matches the corresponding date semantics, and invalid argument types still raise clear messages that mention the first, second, or third argument of the function.

  '

  ## Acceptance signals

  Expressions like `INTERVAL number * 4 - 20 MONTH + toDate32(''2217-01-01'')` and the matching subtraction forms produce correct `Date32` values, and `Date32` interval math no longer diverges from the behavior users already expect from ordinary dates.

Keep locked sections short.
5. If you see working-tree changes you did not make, leave them alone — never revert, stash, or clean them.
6. Commit each requirement IMMEDIATELY after finishing its edits, before starting the next slug.

If a requirement is genuinely unimplementable as stated, still make the best-faith minimal change matching its intent so a meaningful non-empty diff exists, and note that in your report.

title: Use copy for some operations instead of hardlinks
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using zero-copy replication on remote storage can lose safety guarantees when certain maintenance flows rely on hardlinks for files that should really be copied. In those cases different parts can end up sharing blob-tracking paths, which makes later mutations, detach operations, or cleanup race against the wrong remote objects.


  ## Desired outcome

  For the affected MergeTree operations, ClickHouse should copy the files that must remain independent instead of hardlinking them, while preserving hardlinks where they are still safe. This is especially important for zero-copy replication scenarios where detached parts, mutations, and backup-style flows must not reuse bookkeeping paths that belong to another part.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Zero-copy replication workflows no longer rely on unsafe hardlinks for the sensitive files identified by the storage layer, and remote object ownership remains stable across mutation and detach paths. Existing data access semantics stay the same; the change is about correctness and durability of internal storage operations.

title: 'Fix after #40420'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Filesystem-cache state must be internally consistent from the moment a fully downloaded file segment is created, otherwise later readers can misinterpret that segment.

  ## Desired outcome

  A segment created in the `DOWNLOADED` state should initialize all downloaded-state markers consistently instead of leaving one boolean behind in the wrong value.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When the initial state is `DOWNLOADED`, the segment must behave as already downloaded in every subsequent check, including the flag used by completion and read paths.

  '
title: Fix race between DROP and short form of ATTACH
category: bugfix
requirement: 'A user relying on the short ATTACH TABLE db.table syntax should not lose a race against a concurrent DROP or DETACH that changes the table metadata underneath the attach. ClickHouse needs to hold the DDL lock across both metadata lookup and the attach operation for that short syntax, so the attach either sees a consistent table definition or waits properly. The desired outcome is race-free behavior for metadata-based ATTACH TABLE.

  '
title: 'docs: mention SYNC modifier for DROP and DETACH statements'
category: docs
requirement: 'Documentation for `DROP` and `DETACH` should make it obvious that operators can request synchronous completion with the `SYNC` modifier. Readers should not have to infer that behavior from examples or server logs; the statement reference should explain when `SYNC` is available and what waiting for completion means in practice.

  '

title: Do not try to strartup dropped replica
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  During restart or upgrade, a dropped `ReplicatedMergeTree` replica should not be treated like a normal replica that still needs full initialization.

  ## Desired outcome

  If the replica''s ZooKeeper `/host` node is missing, ClickHouse should treat that replica as dropped, keep the table read-only, and avoid the broken startup path that led to failures in this state.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The missing `/host` node must serve as the dropped-replica sentinel, the table should enter read-only mode with a warning instead of trying full startup, and unsupported direct upgrades from 20.3 or older to 22.9 or newer should fail with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` and an intermediate-upgrade requirement.

  '
title: Fix drop of completely dropped table
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In replicated MergeTree cleanup flows, a table can already be fully dropped by the time another server checks its shared metadata. That leaves operators with a follow-up failure while trying to resolve a shared table identifier for something that no longer exists.


  ## Desired outcome

  Dropping a table that has already been completely removed should finish gracefully instead of failing during shared-ID lookup. If ZooKeeper metadata is gone and there is no usable shared identifier, ClickHouse should treat that as an already-dropped state rather than as a new error.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Repeat or late-arriving drop work on an already removed replicated table no longer produces an avoidable failure. Genuine metadata problems still surface normally, but the fully dropped case is handled as a no-op cleanup path.

  '
title: Fix race in `IColumn::dumpStructure`
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Developers and support engineers use `dumpStructure` to inspect complex columns while debugging concurrent workloads, including `LowCardinality` columns.

  ## Desired outcome

  Calling `dumpStructure` from multiple threads on the same column should be race-free and produce a deterministic description instead of intermittent corruption or mismatched nested details.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Repeated concurrent calls return the same stable structure string for the same column instance, including `ColumnLowCardinality` layouts.

  '
title: Support for DWARF-5 in in house DWARF parser
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators debugging production failures with binaries built by newer toolchains need ClickHouse to understand modern debug information formats well enough to recover useful stack traces.


  ## Desired outcome

  The in-house DWARF parser should handle DWARF-5 forms and attributes that appear in those binaries so symbol, file, and line resolution continues to work instead of dropping frames or failing to parse the debug data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Binaries that emit DWARF-5 debug info produce usable stack-trace symbolization, and older supported debug-info formats continue to work as before.

  '

=== exception-message-wording ===
title: Fix incorrect exception message
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When ClickHouse rejects an HTTP-related operation, operators depend on the exception text to understand what actually went wrong, so even a small wording mistake can misdirect troubleshooting.


  ## Desired outcome

  Correct the affected exception message so it describes the real failure condition instead of pointing users at the wrong diagnosis.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The raised exception now uses accurate wording for the failure, making logs and client-visible errors trustworthy again.

  '

=== executable-table-settings ===
title: add settings for executable table func
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Users of the `executable` table function sometimes need to tune execution settings per invocation, but today that call shape is too rigid and forces them to choose between settings and the existing input-query forms.

  ## Desired outcome

  Allow `executable` to accept an optional `SETTINGS` clause while preserving the established forms for literal structure strings, computed structure expressions, and one or more source subqueries.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries such as `executable(..., SETTINGS ...)` work naturally, existing `executable` calls keep working, and callers can still pass structure definitions and source queries in the supported combinations.

  '

=== exists-analyzer-edge-case ===
title: 'Fix #43478'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users can write deeply nested or unusual `EXISTS` queries, and the analyzer should still handle them as regular SQL rather than tripping over an internal edge case.

  ## Desired outcome

  The fuzzer-discovered `EXISTS` scenario should analyze cleanly or fail with an ordinary user-facing SQL error, not with an internal analyzer exception.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The problematic `EXISTS` pattern no longer triggers the regression in query analysis.

  '

=== expired-column-ttl-merges ===
title: Fix bug with multiple TTL merges on expired column
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using column TTLs on `MergeTree` tables can hit failures during repeated vertical TTL merges after a column has already expired, including errors such as `Cannot unlink file ... No such file or directory.`

  ## Desired outcome

  Repeated TTL merges should treat already-expired column files as normal state and continue the merge safely.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Multiple TTL merges on an expired column no longer fail with missing-file cleanup errors, and the merge completes successfully.

  '

=== expired-parts-deletion-priority ===
title: Priority is given to deleting completely expired Parts
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  When multiple TTL actions are eligible, operators expect ClickHouse to reclaim space by removing fully expired parts first, especially under disk pressure. The current selection order can spend effort elsewhere and delay the most obvious cleanup.


  ## Desired outcome

  Prioritize deletion of completely expired parts and avoid letting those fully expired parts distort the reserved-space estimate used for merge planning.


  ## Acceptance signals

  TTL processing chooses fully expired parts for deletion before less-direct TTL work in the affected scenario, and reserved disk-space calculations do not keep those already-expired parts in the estimate.

  '

=== explain-doc-refresh ===
title: Update explain.md
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse users rely on the `EXPLAIN` documentation to understand which form to use and what output to expect before they change queries or investigate plans.


  ## Desired outcome

  Refresh the `EXPLAIN` docs so they describe the current behavior accurately and do not send readers down a stale or misleading path.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reader following the updated page can choose the right `EXPLAIN` form and the wording matches the product as it behaves today.

  '

=== expression-parser-segfault ===
title: Fix possible segfault in expression parser
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user entering malformed or edge-case expressions should receive a normal parse failure, not a segmentation-fault-style server failure inside the expression parser.


  ## Desired outcome

  The expression parser should guard the affected parsing path so invalid input is handled safely and results in an ordinary exception.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The problematic expression no longer brings down the parser path, and valid expressions continue to parse exactly as before.

  '

title: Improve 02354_distributed_with_external_aggregation_memory_usage
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse maintainers need regression coverage for distributed external aggregation memory usage to be stable enough to trust in CI. A flaky test around this scenario wastes triage time and obscures real regressions.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `02354_distributed_with_external_aggregation_memory_usage` coverage should be tightened so it still exercises the intended memory-usage scenario but runs deterministically in automated test environments.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The test continues to validate the same external-aggregation behavior without introducing product changes, and CI no longer fails intermittently because of avoidable timing or assertion instability in that scenario.

  '
title: Add very explicit logging on disk choice for fetch
category: feature
requirement: 'Operators debugging replicated-part fetch placement need logs that explain which disk ClickHouse chose and why. When a fetch uses an explicit disk, falls back to a reservation, or evaluates zero-copy-capable disks, the logs should spell out the selected disk name and disk type so storage-policy decisions are visible after the fact. If a zero-copy fetch fails because the unique id is missing, that error should also mention the disk type to make the failure actionable.

  '
title: Fix big memory usage for fetch.
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When one replica fetches a very large part from another, operators expect replication to stream the data without consuming excessive memory. Fetching a part that includes a huge materialized string column should not cause the receiver to hit memory limits during an otherwise ordinary recovery.


  ## Desired outcome

  The fetch path should keep memory usage bounded while receiving large parts, so replication can complete successfully even for oversized files. After the fetch, `system.replication_queue.last_exception` should remain empty for memory-limit failures instead of recording a `%Memory limit%` exception.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A replica can fetch a large part without a memory spike proportional to the file size, the replication queue finishes the task successfully, and `last_exception` does not contain a memory-limit error for that fetch.

  '

title: Remove trash from Field
category: refactor
requirement: 'This is internal cleanup in ClickHouse''s value-container layer, but it touches code paths that surface in normal SQL execution. The implementation should be simplified so fixed-size, string, tuple, and other field representations are handled consistently without changing existing query results, insert behavior, or exported formats. In particular, current observable behavior for operations like low-cardinality inserts and format writers must remain unchanged while the internals are cleaned up.

  '
title: Remove some methods
category: refactor
requirement: 'Developers integrating with ClickHouse internals should have one clear and consistent way to read values from Field objects. Code that previously relied on free helpers like get<T>(field) and safeGet<T>(field) should move to field.get<T>() and field.safeGet<T>() instead, without changing the underlying behavior. The outcome is an API cleanup that keeps value access semantics the same while removing the old helper style.

  '
title: Fix error message
category: bugfix
requirement: 'When file-cache configuration is invalid, the resulting exception should describe the problem cleanly instead of showing a confusing or misleading message. Operators need validation errors they can act on immediately when bringing up a cache-backed configuration. The desired outcome is clearer configuration diagnostics, with no change to the underlying validation rules.

  '
title: FileCache.cpp tiny refactor
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  The file-cache implementation has accumulated helper logic in a layout that is harder to navigate than necessary, even though the actual runtime behavior is already correct.

  ## Desired outcome

  This cleanup should reorganize the `FileCache` implementation for readability and maintainability without changing cache semantics, settings, or user-visible behavior.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Helper methods around query context management may be moved and constructor initialization order may be cleaned up, but the public `FileCache` behavior and all runtime contracts must remain unchanged.

  '

title: Infer Object type only when allow_experimental_object_type is enabled
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users parsing JSON input can unexpectedly get `Object` inference even when `allow_experimental_object_type` is disabled. That exposes an experimental type in workflows that explicitly chose not to enable it.


  ## Desired outcome

  Automatic `Object` inference must be gated by `allow_experimental_object_type`. If that setting is off, JSON type inference should not synthesize `Object` columns and should fall back to the non-experimental behavior instead.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Turning off `allow_experimental_object_type` is enough to prevent `Object` inference during JSON format processing, while users who intentionally enable the setting continue to get the experimental inference path.

  '
title: Make massages about GCC fatal
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Build engineers need configuration-time diagnostics from GCC to stop the build when they indicate an unsupported or broken setup, because warning-only handling can leave the tree in a misleading half-configured state.


  ## Desired outcome

  Treat the targeted GCC messages as fatal during configuration so unsupported compiler situations are surfaced immediately.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The build stops as soon as the affected GCC diagnostic appears, and engineers are no longer left with a partially configured environment that fails later for less obvious reasons.

  '
title: Remove cruft about gcc
category: refactor
requirement: 'ClickHouse maintainers need to remove obsolete GCC-specific workaround code without changing storage behavior that users already depend on. Disk operations, StorageLog reads and writes, and other existing observable behavior must remain identical after the cleanup even though old compiler-compatibility scaffolding is deleted. The goal is internal codebase simplification only.

  '

title: More generic check for MergeTree table family
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users expect `DELETE` support checks to apply uniformly across the MergeTree family rather than depending on a narrow list of engine names. When the check is too specific, compatible table engines can be rejected even though they share the same intended capabilities.


  ## Desired outcome

  The logic that identifies MergeTree-family tables for `DELETE` handling should be generalized so all relevant MergeTree variants are recognized consistently.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Supported MergeTree-family engines pass the same `DELETE` eligibility check without needing engine-specific special cases, and engines outside that family are still rejected as before.

  '
title: Update geo.md
category: other
requirement: 'This is a documentation-only update for ClickHouse''s geo data type guidance. The published docs should reflect the current supported behavior and remove outdated or misleading material, with no corresponding change to SQL execution or storage behavior. Users reading the reference should get an accurate description of the current product state.

  '
title: Fix getauxval for sanitizer builds
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Very early process startup on sanitizer builds happens before sanitizer runtime interception is fully initialized, but ClickHouse still needs `getauxval`-style information during that phase. If the compatibility implementation calls intercepted reads too early, sanitizer builds can misbehave before the server even starts.


  ## Desired outcome

  The musl-compatible `getauxval` path should read auxiliary-vector data via a direct syscall, and memory-sanitized builds should explicitly unpoison the buffer before inspecting it. This must preserve the same functional result for callers while making startup safe under sanitizers.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Sanitizer builds can obtain auxiliary-vector values during early initialization without tripping over intercepted `read` behavior, and MemorySanitizer no longer sees the parsed auxv buffer as poisoned before it is examined.

  '
title: Enable SQL function getOSKernelVersion() on all platforms
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Cross-platform users and test suites expect the same server-information functions to exist regardless of operating system whenever the underlying information can still be retrieved.

  ## Desired outcome

  Make `getOSKernelVersion` available on all supported platforms rather than only on Linux so portable SQL can query the kernel version consistently.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The SQL function `getOSKernelVersion` is registered outside Linux-only builds and returns the operating system''s kernel version string where ClickHouse runs.

  '

category: other
requirement: 'Users composing bitmap aggregation states should get a normal argument error when they pass the wrong aggregate state into `groupBitmap*`, not a server crash. If the input state was produced by some other aggregate function, ClickHouse should reject it as `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` and clearly point to the bad argument type. The goal is robust validation around aggregate-state chaining instead of undefined behavior.

title: Fix bug in HadoopSnappyReadBuffer
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users reading Hadoop-framed Snappy data expect the decoder to consume a compressed block fully even when one call to the underlying buffer does not provide all required input at once.

  ## Desired outcome

  `HadoopSnappyReadBuffer` should keep feeding the decoder until it no longer reports `NEEDS_MORE_INPUT`, rather than stopping early and producing truncated or incorrect output.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A block that spans multiple input windows must be decoded correctly, repeated `NEEDS_MORE_INPUT` results must be handled inside one logical read, and the regression hash for the reproduced sample must become `673e5b065186cec146789451c2a8f703`.

  '

title: Fix incorrect saved_block_sample with multiple disjuncts in hash join
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts using hash joins with disjunctive join conditions depend on the saved right-side sample block to preserve the correct non-key column structure. With multiple disjuncts, the current logic can keep an outdated column definition and produce incorrect downstream behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a right-side column name already exists in the saved sample block, hash join initialization should refresh that existing entry instead of silently leaving the stale version in place. This should make multi-disjunct joins preserve the right block sample accurately without changing the SQL feature surface.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For joins that produce multiple candidate definitions of the same non-key column name, the saved sample ends up with the latest intended column metadata rather than the first stale copy, and previously incorrect behavior in those disjunctive hash-join cases disappears.

  '
title: Improve hash table preallocation optimisation
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators running large `GROUP BY` queries want hash-table preallocation to help when statistics make it worthwhile, but they do not want the optimization to hurt no-key aggregations or to force an oversized table when the configured budget is too small.


  ## Desired outcome

  Make aggregation preallocation smarter by skipping it for aggregations without keys, skipping it when `max_size_to_preallocate_for_aggregation` is too small to be useful, and raising the default value of `max_size_to_preallocate_for_aggregation` to `100''000''000` for workloads that can benefit.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Keyed aggregations still preallocate when the collected hint is actionable, no-key aggregations start without that optimization, and a too-small preallocation budget no longer causes a slower oversized hash-table path.

  '

title: Fix exception when subquery contains `having` but doesn't contain actual aggregation
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user writing a query with `HAVING` expects it to work only when the query actually uses aggregation, not merely because the clause is present. Right now a subquery that contains `HAVING` but no aggregate functions can be misclassified as an aggregate query, leading to incorrect exceptions or wrong planning in otherwise valid statements.


  ## Desired outcome

  `HAVING` should not by itself force aggregate-query handling. Queries such as `select number from numbers_mt(10) having number >= 9` should behave like ordinary filtered queries, while genuinely aggregate expressions such as `select count() from numbers_mt(100) having count() > 1` must continue to work as aggregate queries.

Process each slug independently, in order:

2. Locate the relevant code with Grep/Glob/Read. The requirement's Context / Desired outcome / Acceptance signals describe a real change that was made to this codebase — infer the concrete minimal edit (source code, config, docs, tests, CI workflows, build files, etc.). Keep changes minimal, consistent with surrounding style, and scoped to the requirement. Do NOT try to build the whole project (far too slow); at most run quick targeted checks (python scripts, grep-based verification, a fast unit-level compile of a single file if truly needed). Some requirements are release bookkeeping (version_date.tsv, changelogs, SECURITY.md), some are doc/test-only edits, some are small C++ fixes or cleanups — judge from the text.
3. Commit that requirement — and only that requirement — with this exact pattern:
   cd /workspace && flock /tmp/ch_git.lock bash -c 'git add <file1> <file2> ... && mkdir -p requirement_patches && git diff --cached > requirement_patches/<slug>.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: <slug>"'
   Rules:
   - NEVER run `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git add -u`, and never stage files you did not change for THIS requirement.
   - The requirement_patches/<slug>.diff file itself must never be staged or committed.
   - After committing, verify requirement_patches/<slug>.diff is non-empty (use `wc -c`). An empty diff means the requirement does not count as complete. If empty, your change did not alter any tracked file — make a real change and recommit. Never leave an empty .diff file.
   - If the git command fails (lock error, nothing staged, etc.), diagnose and retry.
4. Shared-file safety: if a requirement touches files that many other requirements also touch (e.g. utils/list-versions/version_date.tsv, SECURITY.md, popular docs files, src/Core/Settings.h, CI workflow files), wrap the EDIT plus the stage/diff/commit in ONE flock critical section (script the edit with python3 or sed inside the locked bash -c, then add/diff/commit) so a concurrent agent's half-finished edit to the same file cannot leak into your staged diff. Keep locked sections short.
5. If you see working-tree changes you did not make, leave them alone — never revert, stash, or clean them.
6. Commit each requirement IMMEDIATELY after finishing its edits, before starting the next slug.

If a requirement is genuinely unimplementable as stated, still make the best-faith minimal change matching its intent so a meaningful non-empty diff exists, and note that in your report.

When finished with ALL assigned slugs, reply with a compact per-slug report, one line each: `<slug>: done|blocked — one-line summary`.

=== lost-runner-termination ===
title: Terminate lost runners
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  CI operators need the self-hosted runner fleet to recover automatically when runners disappear or stop heartbeating, otherwise orphaned machines keep capacity occupied and distort operational metrics.


  ## Desired outcome

  Teach the runner cleanup automation to recognize genuinely lost runners and terminate them without waiting for manual intervention, while leaving healthy or recently active runners alone.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Stale runners are removed from the fleet in a timely way, healthy runners are not terminated by mistake, and CI capacity recovers on its own after runner loss.

  '

=== lowcardinality-set-header ===
title: Fix create set with wrong header when data type is lowcardinality
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user relying on `Set` creation from low-cardinality data expects the resulting header to preserve the correct type information instead of being built with a mismatched schema.


  ## Desired outcome

  Creating a `Set` from `LowCardinality` input should produce the correct header for that data type so downstream filtering and membership checks see the expected schema.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `Set` creation from low-cardinality columns no longer produces a wrong header, and queries that consume that set behave the same way they do for equivalent non-low-cardinality inputs.

  '

=== lowcardinality-string-cast ===
title: 'Fix: bad cast from type DB::ColumnLowCardinality to DB::ColumnString'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  String serialization paths are used in many formats and table engines, and they should handle `LowCardinality(String)` data as naturally as plain `String` columns. Today a bulk-serialization path can fail with a bad cast because it assumes the incoming column is already a `ColumnString`.


  ## Desired outcome

  Bulk string serialization should transparently support low-cardinality string columns by materializing them to a full column before accessing `ColumnString` storage. The serialized output must remain the same as for an equivalent plain string column.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When `serializeBinaryBulk` receives a low-cardinality string column, it converts through `convertToFullColumnIfLowCardinality`, writes the same bytes that a full `ColumnString` would produce, and no longer throws a bad cast from `DB::ColumnLowCardinality` to `DB::ColumnString`.

  '

=== lowcardinality-value-decoding ===
title: Fix something terribly wrong in LowCardinality
category: bugfix
requirement: 'A user reading LowCardinality data through float or boolean access paths should get the actual dictionary value, not the encoded dictionary index by mistake. Conversions and reads as Float32, Float64, and Bool need to resolve through the LowCardinality dictionary so query results match the stored values. The goal is to eliminate a silent correctness bug in these typed reads.

  '

=== lz4-decompression-bounds ===
title: Add bound check to lz4 decompression
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators may encounter corrupted or maliciously malformed compressed data, and ClickHouse must reject that input safely instead of writing past the output buffer during LZ4 decompression. This is especially important in low-level codec code where a single unchecked copy length can turn a bad block into memory corruption.


  ## Desired outcome

  The fast LZ4 decompressor should verify that the computed match copy does not extend beyond the destination buffer and fail cleanly when it would. From a caller''s perspective, malformed payloads should surface as a normal decompression exception rather than unchecked memory writes or sanitizer findings.


  ## Acceptance signals

  If malformed compressed input would make the decoder copy past `output_end`, decompression is rejected instead of proceeding, and a caller going through `codec->decompress` receives an exception for that bad payload rather than silent memory corruption or undefined behavior.

  '

=== lz4-endianness-removal ===
title: 'LZ4_decompress_faster.cpp: remove endianness-dependent code'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Low-level decompression code must produce identical results on every supported architecture, even when the implementation is rewritten to remove machine-endianness assumptions.

  ## Desired outcome

  Remove endianness-dependent logic from the faster LZ4 decompression path so the implementation is more portable while preserving exactly the same decompressed output.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Compressed data decompresses to the same bytes across little-endian and big-endian platforms, with no user-visible format or API change.

  '

=== macos-build ===
title: Fix build on mac osx
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse contributors who build the project on macOS need the current source tree to compile cleanly with the platform toolchain instead of breaking on platform-specific compiler diagnostics.

  ## Desired outcome

  Restore a successful macOS build for the affected wait-for-process path so a normal contributor build works on Darwin without local source edits.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The macOS build no longer fails on this code path, and no user-visible runtime behavior changes beyond regaining a working build on that platform.

  '
