title: Fix drop for KeeperMap
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Dropping a `KeeperMap` table should be resilient to leftover ZooKeeper state from an earlier failed drop, while still protecting shared storage paths from unsafe deletion. If the table node is already gone, the drop should continue; if the path still has children, ClickHouse should fail with a clear message telling the operator to `DETACH` the table if they really want to delete it. The result should be safer and less fragile cleanup behavior for KeeperMap-backed tables.

  '
title: Possible fix for KeeperMap drop
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using `KeeperMap` can hit intermittent failures when a table is being dropped or created concurrently on different servers. Instead of retrying cleanly, ClickHouse can mis-handle disappearing metadata nodes or race with another server that created the same table path first.


  ## Desired outcome

  `KeeperMap` table creation and drop flows should tolerate these ZooKeeper races and retry when metadata nodes vanish mid-operation or when another server wins the create race for the same path. If a table with the same UUID already exists but has different metadata, the operation should still fail clearly instead of silently accepting a mismatched definition.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Concurrent `KeeperMap` create/drop activity no longer leaves operators with fragile race-dependent failures for normal retryable cases. Genuine conflicts still surface as explicit exceptions, while transient `ZNONODE` and `ZNODEEXISTS` races are treated as recoverable.

  '

title: Fix Endian issue in KeeperSnapshotManager for s390x
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators running ClickHouse Keeper on big-endian systems such as s390x expect snapshot loading and compression detection to work exactly as on little-endian machines. A hard-coded magic-number check can misread compressed snapshots on those platforms.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keeper snapshot compression detection should interpret the stored format correctly regardless of host endianness, so compressed snapshots are recognized and restored on s390x.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A zstd-compressed Keeper snapshot is detected correctly on big-endian hardware, and snapshot load behavior matches what users already see on little-endian systems.

  '
title: doc fix
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators configuring external Kerberos authentication need the documentation wording to be precise, because small mistakes in auth docs cause wasted setup time.

  ## Desired outcome

  Correct the Kerberos documentation typo without changing server behavior.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The published authentication guide reads correctly and no longer trips readers with the incorrect term.

  '

src/Parsers/parseIntervalKind.cpp
src/Parsers/ExpressionListParsers.cpp
src/Common/IntervalKind.cpp
src/Functions/toHour.cpp
src/Functions/dateDiff.cpp

title: Try to fix lambda parsing
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Some valid SQL statements that use lambda syntax are rejected because the parser mishandles that form. Users see a parser exception for a query shape that should be accepted.


  ## Desired outcome

  Lambda expressions covered by this regression should parse the same way users expect from the rest of the SQL dialect, without requiring query rewrites.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The previously failing lambda form is accepted by the parser, and it no longer raises a syntax exception for that valid query pattern.

  '
title: Fix multipart upload for large S3 object
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators storing backups or large data objects in S3 expect multipart upload to keep working as object sizes grow, because a failure late in the upload path can invalidate long-running backup or storage jobs.


  ## Desired outcome

  Fix multipart upload handling for large S3 objects so uploads that cross the affected size threshold complete successfully instead of failing partway through.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Large objects can be written to S3 through the multipart path without upload failure, and existing successful small-object behavior remains unchanged.

  '
title: Build latest tags ONLY from master branch
category: test
requirement: 'Container-image publishing should stop treating every branch like the mainline release branch. The `latest` tag must only be generated when the build is for the `master` branch, while other branches and pull requests should continue to publish only their branch- or commit-specific tags. This keeps accidental non-master builds from being discoverable as `latest` and preserves the expected release contract for downstream users.

  '

args.content:
## What is this directory

This directory contains the ANTLR4 grammar (`ClickHouseLexer.g4` and
`ClickHouseParser.g4`) that describes the ClickHouse SQL dialect, together
with the instructions needed to regenerate the C++ parser sources in
`src/Parsers/New` from that grammar. It is developer tooling only: nothing
here is shipped in ClickHouse binaries, and editing files in this directory
never changes the behavior of a released server by itself.

## Prerequisites

To generate source code you need to install locally the `antlr4` binary
(the ANTLR4 tool, which requires a Java runtime). Any recent `antlr4`
release that supports the `Cpp` target works; use the same version as the
generated sources were produced with to keep diffs minimal.

## How to generate source code files from grammar

title: Fix typo and extra dots in exception messages from OverCommitTracker
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators read memory-related exceptions under pressure, often while diagnosing overload or misconfiguration. Typos and duplicated punctuation in `OverCommitTracker` messages make those errors look less trustworthy and harder to grep for accurately.


  ## Desired outcome

  The relevant `OverCommitTracker` exception text should be corrected so it reads cleanly and consistently without changing when the exception is raised.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The malformed wording and extra punctuation are gone from the affected memory-tracking message, while the surrounding error semantics and trigger conditions stay the same.

  '
title: add to page title for search
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Users searching the documentation often rely on the page title shown in browser tabs and search results to understand what page they have opened. When an important topic''s title omits the searched concept, the right documentation page is harder to discover.


  ## Desired outcome

  Update the relevant documentation page title so search users can immediately recognize that the page covers the feature they were looking for. This is documentation discoverability work only and must not change any SQL behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The page title now includes the missing search-relevant wording, making the page easier to find and identify in browser tabs, search results, and navigation history.

  '

title: Better parallel hash JOIN for floats
category: other
requirement: 'A user relying on parallel hash JOIN with floating-point keys should get the same practical matching behavior they expect from normal float hashing, rather than degraded bucketing caused by the weak-hash path. The join pipeline needs to use the float-aware hashCRC32 behavior when updateWeakHash32 processes float values so semantically equal float keys are partitioned consistently during parallel hash JOIN execution. The goal is better correctness and stability for float-key joins, not a new SQL feature.

  '
title: Revert "Parallel distributed insert select from *Cluster table functions"
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Users reading from `s3Cluster` or `hdfsCluster` should not be forced through the distributed insert-select machinery that was meant for remote target tables and breaks those table functions.

  ## Desired outcome

payload.output:
title: Fix memory accounting in case of MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED errors
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators whose queries hit `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` can be left with memory still counted against the thread or query after the failed allocation path, which makes later activity look larger than it really is.

  ## Desired outcome

  Memory accounting should roll back correctly whenever an allocation fails with `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  After a limit-exceeded error, tracked memory returns to the proper value and subsequent queries start from clean accounting.

  '
title: Fix frequent memory drift message and clarify things in comments
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator watching memory diagnostics should not be spammed by misleading memory-drift messages, and should have better observability into allocator purges when investigating memory behavior.


  ## Desired outcome

  The memory-tracking diagnostics should reduce the noisy drift message pattern and expose clearer allocator-purge visibility so operators can distinguish real memory issues from routine allocator behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Memory-drift logging becomes less misleading, allocator purge activity is reflected in the relevant metrics and profiling counters, and normal memory tracking behavior remains unchanged otherwise.

  '

title: Replace MemoryTrackerBlockerInThread to LockMemoryExceptionInThread
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Some internal operations need to finish their bookkeeping even when a user query is close to its memory limit, but fully disabling memory tracking is broader than necessary and weakens protection for the rest of the server.

  ## Desired outcome

  Limit this escape hatch to user-level memory exceptions so internal paths such as logging, query finalization, and part-related maintenance can complete without turning off global memory accounting.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected internal operations can proceed under user-memory pressure, but global allocation tracking and the stronger server-wide safeguards remain in force.

  '
title: Invalid type in where for Merge table (logical error)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user querying a `Merge` table with an invalid filter expression in `PREWHERE` should get a normal user-facing type error instead of an internal logical failure.


  ## Desired outcome

  If the `PREWHERE` filter type is invalid, ClickHouse should raise `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_COLUMN_FOR_FILTER` with a message in the form `Invalid type for filter in PREWHERE: <type>` so the user can correct the query.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Invalid `PREWHERE` filters on `Merge` tables fail with that explicit type error, while valid filters continue to run normally and no internal logical-error path is exposed.

  '

title: Fix setting description
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  The description for `schema_inference_hints` should clearly say that each entry is a column name followed by its type, and that multiple entries are comma-separated, so users do not guess the wrong syntax.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The visible description for `schema_inference_hints` must describe the format as `column_name1 column_type1, column_name2 column_type2, ...`, with name/type pairs separated by a space and entries separated by commas.

  '

title: fix typo
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Maintainers need a small wording correction in the `SELECT` interpreter area so the source text stays clear and consistent.

  ## Desired outcome

  The typo should be fixed without altering any runtime behavior or user-visible contract.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The wording is corrected and query behavior remains identical.

  '
=== select-parser-fuzzer-limits ===
title: check limits for an AST in select parser fuzzer
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Developers use the select parser fuzzer to reproduce parser failures, but it should be constrained by the same AST limits that protect production requests.

  ## Desired outcome

  The fuzzer must stop building pathological trees once normal query AST limits would have rejected them, so fuzzing results reflect real parser boundaries.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Oversized SELECT ASTs are cut off or rejected in the fuzzer the same way they are for regular queries, instead of exploring unrealistic states.

  '
=== self-extracting-exec-rename ===
title: 'Self-extracting: add --exec param, allow compressed to be renamed'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Teams packaging self-extracting binaries need to decide explicitly which bundled file should be executed after decompression, and they should be able to rename the archive without breaking that behavior.

  ## Desired outcome

  The compressor should accept an `--exec` option so callers can mark the executable payload directly, or choose decompression-only output when `--exec=` is empty.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When `--exec=<path>` is provided, that specific bundled file must be treated as the post-extraction executable even if the archive is renamed later; when `--exec=` is empty, decompression must finish without launching anything; and when `--exec` is omitted entirely, the legacy default behavior should remain available.

  '
=== self-extracting-output-copy ===
title: copy self-extracting to output
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Release engineers want the compressed self-extracting ClickHouse binary to appear in published build output once the invocation-path problems are resolved. After the decompressor fix, packaging should once again expose that artifact for downstream distribution.


  ## Desired outcome

  The build output should copy the self-extracting binary into the published artifacts again, restoring the packaging flow for the compressed executable.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Successful builds once more include the self-extracting artifact in output, and downstream consumers can use the packaged executable without needing special invocation workarounds.

  '
=== self-extracting-post-build ===
title: Fix post-build script for building utils/self-extracting-executable/compressor
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Engineers building the self-extracting ClickHouse utilities on different development machines expect the post-build step to be portable. The current script assumes one platform’s `stat` syntax and can fail on macOS even though the build itself succeeded.


  ## Desired outcome

  The post-build flow for the self-extracting compressor should complete successfully on macOS as well as Linux, without changing the produced artifact format.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A macOS build no longer fails in the post-build script because of incompatible `stat` arguments, and successful builds still produce the same compressor utility as before.

  '
=== self-extracting-real-executable-path ===
title: 'Self-extracting: decompressor, extract real path of executable instead of argv[0]'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Users may launch a self-extracting ClickHouse binary through a symlink or by relying on `PATH`, and they expect it to locate and unpack itself correctly either way. Using `argv[0]` as the executable location is not reliable in those cases.


  ## Desired outcome

  The decompressor should resolve the real executable path before reopening or removing the archive, so self-extracting binaries work no matter how they were invoked.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A self-extracting binary started via a symlink or through `PATH` still finds its own image, extracts successfully, and cleans up the correct executable path instead of depending on the original `argv[0]` text.

  '

=== vim-neovim-compatibility ===
title: Fix vim settings (and make it compatible with neovim)
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Contributors expect the repository''s vim settings to work in both Vim and Neovim, because broken editor config adds friction before they even start coding.


  ## Desired outcome

  Adjust the repository-local vim configuration so the intended editing behavior is preserved while remaining compatible with Neovim.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Opening the repository in Neovim no longer trips on the shared config, and standard Vim users keep the same practical editor behavior.

  '
=== waitmutation-zk-queue-race ===
title: Fix the race between waitMutation and updating local queue from ZK
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators waiting on a mutation in a replicated MergeTree table expect `waitMutation` to reflect the local replica’s real state, even while ZooKeeper updates are still arriving. A race in replica ordering can make the wait path report that a mutation was killed or unfinished when the local queue simply has not been checked first.


  ## Desired outcome

  The local replica should be prioritized when evaluating mutation completion so `waitMutation` does not lose to a timing race with queue refreshes from ZooKeeper.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A mutation that has completed locally no longer intermittently reports an `UNFINISHED` or killed-style outcome because another replica was examined first, and waiting behavior is stable under ordinary replication lag.

  '
=== web-disk-missing-file-sigsegv ===
title: Fix possible SIGSEGV for web disks when file does not exists
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using web-backed disks may probe for files that are missing, and they expect a normal "not found" answer rather than an exception caused by walking past the end of the in-memory file list. Today a missing path can trigger a segmentation-fault-class failure instead of a clean absence check.


  ## Desired outcome

  File-existence checks for web disks should return `false` when the requested path is not present, even when the lower-bound lookup lands at the end of the available file list. Missing remote files must be handled as an expected condition, not as a low-level failure in metadata traversal.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A lookup for a non-existent web-disk path safely reports that the file is absent, while existing-prefix checks continue to work as before and no out-of-bounds iterator access is triggered by the missing-path case.

  '
=== website-dead-code-removal-2 ===
title: Remove old code from the website (part 2)
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  After an initial website cleanup, maintainers still need a second pass to remove more dead code from the older site implementation. This should reduce repository weight and maintenance burden without changing the supported site experience.


  ## Desired outcome

  Additional obsolete website scripts and assets should be removed, while preserving the current site-generation behavior that users and docs readers still rely on.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The second batch of legacy website code is no longer present, and the remaining supported website tooling continues to produce the same published experience.

  '
=== website-dead-code-removal ===
title: Remove old code from the website
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Website maintainers need the ClickHouse site codebase to contain only the paths and assets that are still part of the published experience. Carrying a large block of dead website code makes maintenance and future cleanup harder without helping users.


  ## Desired outcome

  Obsolete website implementation code should be removed while preserving the current published site behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The unused legacy website code is gone from the repository, and the supported site-generation flow continues to work without relying on those removed files.

  '
=== welchttest-argument-error ===
title: Fix logical error from welchTTest
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user calling `welchTTest` with inputs that produce an invalid number of degrees of freedom should get a proper argument error rather than an internal logical failure.


  ## Desired outcome

  When the p-value cannot be computed because the derived degrees of freedom are invalid, `welchTTest` should fail with a user-facing `BAD_ARGUMENTS` exception and the message `Cannot calculate p_value, because the t-distribution has inappropriate value of degrees of freedom (={}). It should be > 0`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Invalid Welch''s t-test inputs now produce that explicit argument error, and valid `welchTTest` calls continue to return the same statistical results as before.

  '
=== window-order-read-setting ===
title: 'Query plan optimization setting: read in window order'
category: other
requirement: 'Query planning for window functions should be controllable instead of being an all-or-nothing implicit optimization. Add a user-facing optimization setting named `reuse_storage_ordering_for_window_functions` so operators can explicitly allow or disable reading data in storage order for window-function execution, and make that choice visible in planning and `EXPLAIN` output instead of silently hard-wiring the optimization.

  '

1	title: Relax "too many parts" threshold
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Large MergeTree partitions with very large parts can still hit the generic `Too many parts` protections even when the part sizes show that the table is merging effectively and handling a legitimately huge dataset. That forces operators to choose between unsafe global threshold increases and unnecessary insert throttling.

=== try-base58-decode ===
title: Add function tryBase58Decode()
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  SQL users already have a forgiving `tryBase64Decode` path, but Base58 decoding still forces them into exception-driven handling when incoming data may be malformed. That makes ingestion and cleanup queries harder to write when invalid Base58 strings should simply produce a null result.


  ## Desired outcome

  Add a `tryBase58Decode` function that mirrors the tolerant behavior of `tryBase64Decode`: valid Base58 strings decode normally, and invalid values do not raise an exception. The Base58 decode family should also expose a consistent one-argument contract, so incorrect arity is rejected with the usual `Wrong number of arguments for function {}: 1 expected.` message.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Users can call `tryBase58Decode` in SQL to handle mixed-quality input without aborting the query on bad Base58 data. The Base58 and Base64 conversion functions keep a consistent single-argument calling convention and clear argument-validation errors.

  '
=== tsan-exit-interception ===
title: Fix TSan errors (correctly ignore _exit interception)
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Developers running ThreadSanitizer builds can hit noise or failures related to `_exit` interception in this path even though the product logic is fine. That makes sanitizer runs less trustworthy and harder to use.


  ## Desired outcome

  Adjust the implementation so TSan builds complete cleanly in this area without changing runtime behavior for ordinary users.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The sanitizer warning tied to `_exit` interception is gone from this path, and non-sanitized runtime behavior stays the same.

  '
=== ttl-expired-parts-logging ===
title: Optimize TTL merge, completely expired parts can be removed in time
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  MergeTree operators use part logs to understand why background merges happened, especially when TTL rules are deleting data or removing expired parts entirely. Today a fully expired TTL cleanup can be hard to distinguish from other merge activity in the log stream.


  ## Desired outcome

  Part-log records should explicitly identify the case where a merge task was scheduled to drop completely expired parts, using a distinct merge-reason value rather than lumping it into the existing TTL categories. This is primarily an observability improvement; merge behavior itself should stay the same.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When TTL cleanup removes fully expired parts, the part log reports a dedicated reason named `TTLDropMerge`, allowing operators to distinguish drop-only TTL work from `TTLDeleteMerge` and `TTLRecompressMerge` in their monitoring and troubleshooting workflows.

  '
=== tuple-in-index-analysis ===
title: Fix index analysis with tuples and `IN`
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users expect tuple-based `IN` predicates to benefit from the same set-index analysis as other searchable conditions, especially when those predicates are important for pruning work in MergeTree queries.

  ## Desired outcome

  Fix tuple handling in set-index analysis so tuple elements get stable internal names and tuple `IN` conditions are analyzed correctly.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries that use tuple `IN` predicates participate in index analysis and pruning as intended, instead of missing the optimization because tuple elements were identified inconsistently.

  '

category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  Typo-correction logic should fall back to a normal analysis error or suggestion path instead of dereferencing a null pointer while collecting visible identifiers.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The same malformed query now returns a regular analyzer exception or hint, not an internal failure during identifier collection.

User-facing messages should read correctly—for example fixing obvious misspellings such as `backward incompatibility`—but no queries, settings, or storage behavior should change beyond those editorial and safety fixes.

15	  '

title: Analyzer SumIfToCountIfPass fix
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users of the experimental analyzer expect query rewrites to preserve semantics when simplifying aggregate expressions.

  ## Desired outcome

  `SumIfToCountIfPass` should only rewrite `sumIf` patterns into `countIf` when the result is truly equivalent, instead of changing answers or types for edge cases that should be left alone.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries affected by this pass return the same results they would have without the optimization, while the safe rewrite opportunities still apply.

  '
=== sumif-rewrite-default-off ===
title: Disable optimize_rewrite_sum_if_to_count_if by default
category: other
requirement: 'A SQL user should not get incorrect results because ClickHouse aggressively rewrites sumIf or sum(if()) into countIf behind the scenes. The optimize_rewrite_sum_if_to_count_if setting should now default to false so this rewrite is disabled unless a user explicitly opts back in. The goal is to favor correctness over an optimization that can change results.

  '
=== summap-null-merge ===
title: Fix merging null values in AggregateFunctionSumMap
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts using `sumMap`, `minMap`, and `maxMap` sometimes aggregate data sets that include `NULL` map values and then ask for `WITH TOTALS`, `ROLLUP`, or `CUBE`.

  ## Desired outcome

  Those aggregate states should merge correctly across grouping levels instead of raising an exception or dropping the `NULL`-carrying rows during totals calculation.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries using these functions with nullable map values return stable grouped results and correct totals for `WITH TOTALS`, `ROLLUP`, and `CUBE`.

  '
=== summingmergetree-lowcardinality-crash ===
title: Fix crash in `SummingMergeTree` with `LowCardinality`
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user aggregating data in `SummingMergeTree` can store numeric values as `LowCardinality`, but merges currently fail when those parts are compacted.

  ## Desired outcome

  `SummingMergeTree` should merge and finalize parts with `LowCardinality` numeric columns exactly as it does for ordinary numeric columns, instead of raising an internal exception during optimization.

  ## Acceptance signals

  After `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL`, rows with the same key are summed correctly and the resulting values remain readable for `LowCardinality(UInt32)`-backed data.

  '
=== suppress-kvm-clock-warning ===
title: Do not warn about kvm-clock
category: other
requirement: 'An operator running ClickHouse inside a virtualized Linux environment should not see a misleading warning that the machine is using a slow clock source when the kernel is actually using kvm-clock. The startup warning should stay suppressed for kvm-clock just as it already is for tsc, and only appear when neither of those clock sources is active. This change is about removing a false performance alarm, not hiding real clock-source problems.

=== symlink-path-detection ===
title: Fix a bug with symlinks detection
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Operators and packagers working with database paths that include symbolic links can have ClickHouse mis-detect whether a path is symlinked, which leads to incorrect safety checks or path handling.

  ## Desired outcome

  Symlink detection should resolve and compare paths correctly across install, database creation, and shared filesystem-helper logic.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Legitimate symlinked paths are identified consistently, non-symlink paths are not misclassified, and the same rules apply across the affected entry points.

  '
=== sync-request-timeout-10 ===
title: Set sync_request_timeout to 10 to avoid reconnections in tests
category: test
requirement: '## Context

  CI maintainers have tests that reconnect unexpectedly because the default sync timeout is too short for the environment in which those checks run.

  ## Desired outcome

  The affected tests should use a larger `sync_request_timeout` so they exercise the intended behavior instead of failing due to reconnect noise.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Those tests run with `sync_request_timeout = 10` and stop producing spurious reconnection failures.

  '

=== s3-key-sharding-2 ===
title: Sharding s3 key names (2)
category: other
requirement: 'Operators storing `Set`, `Join`, log-family, and `MergeTree` data on S3 should not need to care how object keys are laid out underneath the bucket prefix. Sharding S3 key names must stay invisible at the SQL level: reads must survive restarts, partition moves and freezes must keep working, and cleanup operations such as `TRUNCATE`, `DROP`, `UNFREEZE`, and detached-part removal must still delete exactly the right remote objects.

  '
=== s3-multipart-upload-race ===
title: Fix race in s3 multipart upload
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  An operator writing large backups or table data to S3 expects multipart upload to scale up part sizes safely under concurrency without reusing part numbers or overrunning S3’s hard limits. Today the upload path can race when background tasks are assigned part numbers, which can produce invalid multipart state or push an upload past the supported number of parts without a clear configuration error.


  ## Desired outcome

  Multipart uploads should assign part numbers from a single monotonic sequence, grow part size only when that sequence reaches the configured threshold, and fail early with a clear configuration exception if the upload would exceed `max_part_number`. Operators also need `max_part_number` to be a real S3 request setting that can be configured alongside `min_upload_part_size`, `max_upload_part_size`, and the part-size multiply controls.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Concurrent multipart writes no longer derive part numbers from the number of queued background tasks, and oversized uploads raise an `INVALID_CONFIG_PARAMETER` exception that points users to `min_upload_part_size`, `max_upload_part_size`, `upload_part_size_multiply_factor`, `upload_part_size_multiply_parts_count_threshold`, `max_single_part_upload_size`, and `max_part_number`. The same request-setting defaults are used consistently across S3-backed features such as backups, object storage disks, and snapshot uploads.'
=== s3-operation-logging ===
title: More logging for S3
category: other
requirement: 'Object-storage and replicated-part workflows should emit richer logs around S3 reads, writes, and part exchange so operators can diagnose failures without turning on ad hoc debug instrumentation. The additional logging should make it easier to see which request, key, or part lifecycle step is in progress while preserving the normal data path.

  '
=== s3-part-move-parallel-write ===
title: Revert revert 41268 disable s3 parallel write for part moves to disk s3
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator moving parts to an S3-backed volume with TTL or `ALTER ... MOVE` needs those moves to complete without exhausting memory on large parts.


  ## Desired outcome

  Part moves to S3-backed storage should use the restored parallel-write path so data can be moved efficiently, but memory usage during those moves must stay bounded and should not run into `Memory limit` failures for the covered scenario.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Moving a partition to an external S3 volume succeeds without the old excessive-memory pattern, peak memory stays within the expected bounded range during the move, and no `Memory limit` error is recorded for the operation.

  '
=== s3-plain-drop-tables ===
title: Allow to "drop tables" from s3_plain disk (so as from web disk)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using immutable or write-once storage such as `s3_plain` still need normal DDL lifecycle commands when managing restored or attached tables.

  ## Desired outcome

  `DROP TABLE` and follow-on cleanup workflows should succeed for tables placed on `s3_plain` without trying to delete underlying remote objects that are intentionally not removable.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Tables on `s3_plain` can be dropped like tables on `web`, and disk metadata exposed through `system.disks` correctly reflects readonly and drop-related capabilities.

  '
=== s3-plain-storage-type ===
title: changed type name for s3 plain storage
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators use `system.disks` as a contract for distinguishing storage backends during backup, restore, and troubleshooting. Reporting `S3PlainObjectStorage` as plain `s3` hides an important behavioral distinction and makes inventory checks ambiguous.


  ## Desired outcome

  Disks backed by the plain S3 object-storage mode should advertise a distinct type string `s3_plain` instead of reusing `s3`, while ordinary S3-backed disks continue to report `s3`. This naming distinction should flow through the system tables that operators inspect during backup and restore validation.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `system.disks` shows plain S3 disks with type `s3_plain`, standard S3 disks still report `s3`, and mixed backup/restore setups can reliably distinguish entries such as `disk_s3_plain` from the normal S3-backed disks in the same cluster.

  '
=== s3-request-timeout ===
title: Increase request_timeout_ms for s3 disks.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator writing large parts to S3-compatible disks such as MinIO expects multipart uploads to survive the long finalization phase instead of timing out while the object store is still responding.

  ## Desired outcome

  The default S3 disk request timeout should be long enough for `Complete Multipart Upload` to finish under normal large-upload conditions and heartbeat traffic. Operators should not have to override `request_timeout_ms` immediately just to make standard large part uploads reliable.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The default `request_timeout_ms` for S3 disks is increased to `30000`, and large multipart upload completion is no longer cut off by the former 5-second default.

  '

=== mv-query-context-leak ===
title: Fix memory leak while pushing to MVs w/o query context (from Kafka/...)
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users ingesting from Kafka and similar background pipelines often push data into materialized views without a normal query context, and those flows should not leak memory over time.


  ## Desired outcome

  Background read and write tasks should attach and detach thread-level query state safely even when the originating path has no ordinary query context, so pushing into materialized views stays leak-free.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Long-running background ingestion into materialized views does not accumulate leaked query/thread state, and the existing data flow keeps working.

  '
=== mysql-interface-docs ===
title: Improve the MySQL interface usage description
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  People connecting to ClickHouse through the MySQL protocol need the documentation to show the correct settings and example command line. Small mistakes in these instructions turn a simple compatibility path into a frustrating setup exercise.


  ## Desired outcome

  Improve the MySQL interface usage documentation so it describes the right setting approach and shows a correct `mysql` client command example. This is a documentation usability fix, not a protocol change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reader can follow the docs and connect with the MySQL client using the documented settings and command format without having to guess missing details.

  '
=== mysql-odbc-archive-url ===
title: Change mysql-odbc url
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Integration environments break unnecessarily when they download build dependencies from vendor URLs that later move or disappear, even though the product itself has not changed.

  ## Desired outcome

  Point the MySQL ODBC dependency fetch to a stable archived location so building the integration image does not depend on a transient download URL remaining live.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The integration base image can still retrieve the required MySQL ODBC package from the maintained archive path without any user-facing database behavior change.

  '
=== named-collections-clickhouse-example ===
title: Doc. Example named-collections + clickhouse database
category: docs
requirement: '## Context

  Users adopting named collections need a concrete example for connecting to another ClickHouse database, not just object storage and external-service examples.

  ## Desired outcome

  The named-collections documentation should include a complete remote-ClickHouse example with the keys operators actually need and show how that collection is used from `remote`, `remoteSecure`, and `cluster`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The doc must show a named collection containing `host`, `port`, `database`, `user`, and `password`, and the terminology in that page should consistently say named collections rather than named connections.

  '
=== negative-float-datetime64 ===
title: Fix toDateTime64() for negative floats
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users converting negative floating-point values to `DateTime64` can get inconsistent results compared with the equivalent negative integer inputs. The function should not behave differently just because the same timestamp value was written as a float.


  ## Desired outcome

  `toDateTime64` should produce the same timestamp for equivalent negative integer and negative floating-point inputs. Invalid floating-point values such as NaN, infinity, or values outside the supported decimal range should continue to fail explicitly with `DECIMAL_OVERFLOW` instead of producing a silent mis-conversion.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Negative float and negative integer inputs map to the same `DateTime64` result when they represent the same value, and truly invalid float inputs still raise the documented overflow error. Existing positive-value behavior remains unchanged.

  '
=== nested-column-drop-guard ===
title: Prevent dropping nested column if it creates empty part
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A MergeTree user expects `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` to be rejected whenever removing a nested structure would leave existing parts structurally invalid. Right now dropping a `Nested` or `Array(Tuple(...))` parent column can slip through in cases where some parts would become effectively empty or inconsistent, especially after other columns were added.


  ## Desired outcome

  Dropping a nested parent such as `arr` or `nes` should be refused whenever existing data parts still depend on its subcolumns, even if a later schema change added another column to the table. Users should only be allowed to drop that nested structure when the stored parts remain valid after the change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Queries like `ALTER TABLE 02500_nested DROP COLUMN arr` or `ALTER TABLE 02500_nested DROP COLUMN nes` raise `BAD_ARGUMENTS` in the protected cases, both with `flatten_nested = 1` and `flatten_nested = 0`. The same operations still succeed in the explicitly allowed layouts where the remaining parts stay valid.'
=== nested-json-schema-inference ===
title: Fix nested JSON Objects schema inference
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users inferring schema from semi-structured JSON expect nested objects to stay typed as JSON objects instead of being flattened into an overly generic fallback type.


  ## Desired outcome

  If nested object values appear during schema inference, ClickHouse should infer the JSON `Object` type for that structure rather than downgrading the schema just because the values are nested.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Nested JSON objects are inferred as JSON `Object` data, and mixed-but-compatible nested object samples keep the intended object-oriented schema.

  '

=== uint128-quantile-type ===
title: Use correct type for `UInt128` in `AggregateFunctionQuantile`
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user calculating quantiles on `UInt128` data expects those values to be treated as unsigned 128-bit integers throughout the aggregate computation.


  ## Desired outcome

  `AggregateFunctionQuantile` should infer and store the correct `UInt128` value type instead of treating the data as `Int128`, so large unsigned values produce correct quantile results.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Quantile calculations over `UInt128` columns return results based on the true unsigned value range, and the aggregate path no longer suffers from incorrect type interpretation for 128-bit unsigned inputs.

  '

=== uk-price-paid-zh ===
title: 'Doc: add zh translation'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Chinese-speaking ClickHouse user following the example datasets guide should be able to complete the UK property price walkthrough without switching back to the English documentation.

  ## Desired outcome

  The `uk-price-paid` getting-started page in the Chinese docs should contain the full localized tutorial, including table creation, data loading, validation queries, example analyses, and the projection-based performance section, rather than acting as a thin wrapper around English content.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The Chinese documentation page presents a complete standalone walkthrough for the UK Property Price Paid dataset and covers the same end-to-end workflow that readers use in the English guide.

  '

=== unhex-fixedstring-support ===
title: unhex support FixedString arguments
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users expect `unhex` to work on fixed-width binary strings as well as ordinary variable-width strings, but today `FixedString` arguments are rejected unnecessarily. That makes binary-processing queries less ergonomic than they should be.


  ## Desired outcome

  Extend `unhex` so it accepts `FixedString` inputs wherever the existing function already supports string data.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `unhex` succeeds when its argument is `FixedString`, and the output semantics match the existing behavior users already get for ordinary string arguments.

  '

=== uninline-error-handling ===
title: 'Refactoring: Uninline some error handling methods'
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Date and time conversion helpers currently inline a set of error-handling paths that are difficult to follow and maintain. The resulting behavior is correct, but the implementation is more tangled than it needs to be.


  ## Desired outcome

  Refactor these conversion helpers so the error handling is moved out of the hottest inline path while preserving the existing exception contracts for invalid argument types. This is internal maintenance work: functions should still reject the same unsupported types with the same `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` outcomes.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The code is easier to maintain, and users still see the same conversion behavior and the same type-validation failures they saw before the refactor.

  '

=== uniq-injective-elimination ===
title: Analyzer UniqInjectiveFunctionsEliminationPass
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Analysts writing `uniq` queries often wrap keys in injective transformations, even though those wrappers do not change cardinality.

  ## Desired outcome

  The analyzer should recognize injective wrappers inside `uniq`-style aggregation and eliminate the unnecessary work without changing the distinct-count result.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Equivalent `uniq` queries over injective expressions behave the same semantically, but the analyzer can simplify them before execution.

  '

=== unique-query-thread-ids ===
title: Make thread ids in the process list and query_log unique to avoid waste
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator inspecting running queries in the process list or later analyzing `query_log` uses thread identifiers to understand how a query executed.

  ## Desired outcome

  Those thread identifier lists should contain unique thread ids only. Reused worker threads should not be recorded multiple times for the same query, because duplicates waste space and make operational analysis noisier without adding information.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Query status reporting still exposes the thread list, but each thread id appears at most once even when a pooled thread is attached to the same query more than once.

  '

=== unused-constructor-removal ===
title: Remove unused constructor
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context

  Core MergeTree metadata code is performance-sensitive and widely reused, so internal cleanup is valuable only if it does not alter the storage behavior that users rely on.

  ## Desired outcome

  Remove constructor surface that is no longer needed in the index-granularity implementation so the code stays simpler, while keeping all externally observable MergeTree behavior unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Table reads, writes, and index-granularity handling continue to behave as before, with this change acting only as internal cleanup.

  '

title: Add generic implementation for arbitrary structured named collections, access type and system.named_collections
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators and integrations increasingly need reusable named connection settings that are richer than a flat list of simple values, and they also need a supported way to inspect which named collections exist. Today that capability is too limited.


  ## Desired outcome

  Add first-class support for structured named collections and expose them through a discoverable system surface so administrators can inspect and manage them safely.


  ## Acceptance signals

  ClickHouse exposes `system.named_collections` with the collection name and its structured contents, and viewing that inventory is governed by the `SHOW NAMED COLLECTIONS` access type rather than an ad hoc mechanism.

  '
title: Fix style check
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A recent change left the codebase failing the style check even though the intended runtime behavior was fine. This blocks CI and slows down unrelated work.


  ## Desired outcome

  Bring the affected code back into compliance with the project style rules without changing its behavior. This is a narrow correctness-of-formatting fix, not a product change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The style check passes again and the affected code behaves exactly as it did before the formatting repair.

  '

title: Small style fixes
category: bugfix
requirement: 'ClickHouse maintainers need a small internal cleanup in this area without changing any observable SQL behavior, public API contract, or operational semantics. Existing results, error behavior, and integrations should remain the same after the refactor. The goal is code-quality improvement only.

  '
title: Attempt to fix StyleCheck condition
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  CI maintainers depend on `StyleCheck` to cancel and rerun predictably when new commits arrive, because a stuck or duplicated style job wastes capacity and blocks merges for unrelated reasons.


  ## Desired outcome

  Correct the workflow condition so `StyleCheck` follows the intended rerun and cancellation behavior without changing what the check itself validates.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Only the relevant `StyleCheck` run remains active for the current PR state, superseded runs are handled cleanly, and style validation coverage stays the same.

  '

title: stylecheck renewed and version in docker set explicitely
category: feature
requirement: 'Style-check infrastructure should run against a pinned, explicit Docker toolchain version so maintainers get reproducible formatting results instead of depending on whatever image happens to be current. Refreshing the style-check environment must keep the checks themselves unchanged for contributors while making CI output consistent across runs.

  '
title: fix bug when remove unneeded columns in subquery
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Users running queries with subqueries expect column-pruning optimizations to remove only truly unnecessary expressions.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a subquery expression contains aggregate logic, the rewrite pass that removes unneeded columns must keep that expression even if the subquery does not have its own GROUP BY clause.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Subquery pruning no longer drops required aggregate expressions, and the optimized query still returns the correct result.

  '
title: Combining sumIf->countIf and multiIf->if opt.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  SQL users who enable multiple expression optimizations expect those rewrites to compose, instead of one optimization preventing another obviously compatible one from happening.

  ## Desired outcome

  Let the `sumIf` to `countIf` rewrite still apply after `multiIf` has already been simplified to `if`, so eligible queries benefit from both optimizations together.

  ## Acceptance signals

  With both settings enabled, queries shaped like a `sumIf` over a simplified conditional expression receive the combined optimization instead of stopping after the first rewrite.

  '

payload.output:
title: Allow to parse JSON objects into Strings in JSON input formats
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A data engineer ingesting JSON into a `String` column may receive payloads where some fields are plain strings and others are nested JSON objects. Today those object values are rejected or coerced inconsistently, which makes mixed-shape feeds awkward to load even when the downstream requirement is simply to preserve the original JSON text.


  ## Desired outcome

  When the input format setting `input_format_json_read_objects_as_strings` is enabled, JSON input formats should accept object values for `String` targets and store the object as its JSON string representation instead of rejecting it. This should work both when parsing directly into declared `String` columns and when inferring types from JSON input that mixes strings with objects or maps.


  ## Acceptance signals

  With `input_format_json_read_objects_as_strings = 1`, a field containing `{...}` can be loaded into a `String` column and remains readable as serialized JSON text, while the default behavior stays unchanged when the setting is off. The new setting is documented and wired through format settings so users can reliably turn it on anywhere JSON input parsing is used.'
title: Add test for setting output_format_json_validate_utf8
category: feature
requirement: 'This is regression coverage for the existing `output_format_json_validate_utf8` setting rather than a new runtime feature. The JSON-format test suite should explicitly protect the cases where invalid UTF-8 must be rejected or allowed according to that setting, while leaving current execution behavior unchanged. The goal is to prevent future regressions in a user-visible setting that already exists.

  '

title: Add setting to disable limit on kafka_num_consumers
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators sometimes run Kafka-backed tables on hosts where they intentionally want more Kafka consumers than the CPU-core-based safety cap would normally allow.


  ## Desired outcome

  There should be an explicit setting named `kafka_disable_num_consumers_limit` that disables the automatic upper bound tied to available CPU cores, while leaving the existing safety check in place by default for everyone else.


  ## Acceptance signals

  When `kafka_disable_num_consumers_limit` is enabled, `kafka_num_consumers` can exceed the usual core-derived cap; when it is not enabled, the previous limit enforcement still applies.

  '
title: Fix keeper-bench in case of error during scheduling a thread
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Engineers using `keeper-bench` to stress Keeper can hit an error while scheduling worker threads, and the benchmark tool may not shut down cleanly after that failure.

  ## Desired outcome

  Thread-scheduling failures should trigger the normal shutdown path so the tool exits predictably without leaving workers hanging.

  ## Acceptance signals

  If thread scheduling fails during a run, `keeper-bench` marks shutdown, waits for cleanup, and then re-raises the original error instead of hanging.

  '
title: Increase some logging level for keeper client.
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators debugging Keeper connectivity often need key client-side messages to appear at a more visible log level, because a too-quiet default makes intermittent coordination issues much harder to diagnose in production.


  ## Desired outcome

  Promote the relevant Keeper-client messages so important connection and retry information is available without turning on excessively verbose logging everywhere else.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected Keeper-client events now show up at a practical log level during troubleshooting, giving operators enough context to diagnose failures from ordinary logs.

  '

title: Block memory tracker in Keeper during commit
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators running ClickHouse Keeper under write load need commit processing to be robust even when memory accounting is active. Internal bookkeeping during commit should not trigger avoidable memory-tracker interference that surfaces as operational instability.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keeper should block or isolate memory tracking during the sensitive commit path so ordinary commit processing does not fail because of internal accounting noise.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Commit-heavy Keeper workloads continue to behave the same from a client perspective, but the affected commit path no longer reports spurious memory-tracker-related failures.

  '
title: Faster commit in Keeper
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Keeper throughput is heavily influenced by how much bookkeeping happens while a transaction commit is being finalized. Clearing too much cached node state at commit time adds avoidable overhead, especially when many nodes were touched but only a subset actually became stable at that zxid.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keeper should make commit processing cheaper by only revisiting cached nodes whose paths have no further modifications in the current transaction, instead of scanning and clearing unrelated cache entries wholesale. This must preserve correctness of the node cache while reducing commit-time work.


  ## Acceptance signals

  During `commit`, Keeper tracks only the paths that stop changing at the committed zxid, removes cached entries for those paths when appropriate, and avoids the broader cache sweep that previously made commit processing slower under write-heavy workloads.

  '

=== profile-events-tracing ===
title: Fix tracing of profile events
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator who enables `trace_profile_events` to diagnose slow or unstable queries needs tracing to stay informative without creating feedback loops inside the tracing machinery itself. Right now some internal profile events generated while profiling or handling failed writes can recursively enter the trace log again, which makes stress runs noisy and can destabilize the very diagnostics people turned on.


  ## Desired outcome

  Tracing should still report normal query-level profile events, but internal bookkeeping events such as `QueryProfilerSignalOverruns` and write failures that are counted only for observability must be recorded without sending those same counters back into the trace log. In other words, operators should be able to leave `trace_profile_events` enabled during heavy profiling and failed-write scenarios without seeing self-generated trace spam or re-entrant logging side effects.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A long-running query with `trace_profile_events = 1` still completes and produces trace data, while the internal counters that track profiler overruns or discard-on-failure writes are incremented through the non-tracing path instead of being re-emitted into the trace log. The public contract should make that distinction explicit by using `incrementNoTrace` for events that must never recurse into tracing.'
=== profileevents-spill-descriptions ===
title: Add doc to ExternalSort/Agg/Join ProfileEvents
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Operators using external sort, aggregation, and join spill paths rely on ProfileEvents to understand why queries touched disk, but unnamed counters are hard to interpret in dashboards and incident reports.


  ## Desired outcome

  The external-spill ProfileEvents should carry real human-readable descriptions so users can tell what `ExternalSortWritePart`, `ExternalSortMerge`, `ExternalAggregationWritePart`, `ExternalAggregationMerge`, `ExternalJoinWritePart`, and `ExternalJoinMerge` are counting.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The relevant external sort, aggregation, and join ProfileEvents expose descriptive text about temporary files and merge streams, and existing metric names stay stable.

  '
=== progress-result-rows-bytes ===
title: Add result_rows and result_bytes to progress reports
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Clients that watch query progress over HTTP or other progress-reporting channels currently see how much data was read or written, but they cannot tell how many result rows and bytes have already been produced.

  ## Desired outcome

  Extend progress reporting to include `result_rows` and `result_bytes`, so client applications can monitor output production in the same stream as the existing read/write counters.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Progress payloads include the exact fields `result_rows` and `result_bytes`, and they are emitted even in JSON progress messages where users already consume the other progress counters.

  '
=== projection-alter-update-columns ===
title: Fix for missing columns bug with projections an ALTER UPDATE
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  After certain `ALTER UPDATE` operations, queries that would otherwise use a projection can fail because required columns are no longer tracked correctly through the projection path. Users see missing-column errors in a workflow that should continue to work.


  ## Desired outcome

  Projection planning should preserve every column needed by the final query when altered data and projection ordering interact, so those reads continue to succeed.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected projection query no longer fails with a missing-column error after `ALTER UPDATE`, and the planner keeps the required columns available through the projection read path.

  '
=== projection-fetch-cleanup ===
title: Fix `LOGICAL_ERROR` if fetch of projection was stopped
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  An operator using zero-copy replication with projections expects a cancelled or interrupted fetch to clean up safely instead of leaving broken partial state behind. Today, if fetching a projection stops midway, ClickHouse can throw a `LOGICAL_ERROR` during cleanup because projection files and transaction state are not rolled back consistently.


  ## Desired outcome

  If downloading a replicated part or any of its projections is interrupted, ClickHouse should clean up the partially fetched files and commit the cleanup transaction without raising a secondary internal error. The failure should remain a normal fetch interruption, not escalate into a misleading `LOGICAL_ERROR` about projection handling.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The zero-copy projection cancellation scenario in replicated MergeTree no longer reports the previous `LOGICAL_ERROR`; instead the partial base part or `.proj` data is removed through the proper cleanup path. Operators can still rely on the fetch failing when interrupted, but not on lingering broken state afterward.'
=== projection-md-docs ===
title: Update projection.md
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators and developers read the projection-alteration docs to understand what is and is not supported when managing projections on live tables. If the page is incomplete or misleading, people may expect commands to work that are not actually part of the product contract.


  ## Desired outcome

  Clarify the projection documentation so it accurately describes the supported `ALTER ... PROJECTION` workflows and their limitations from a user''s perspective. This is a docs-only change and should not modify SQL semantics or projection behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The projection documentation gives clearer, more accurate guidance about supported operations and expectations, and users can rely on the page without encountering a mismatch between the docs and current ClickHouse behavior.

  '

  '

=== offset-pipeline-termination ===
title: Fix possible pipeline stuck exception for queries with OFFSET
category: bugfix
requirement: 'Queries that use `OFFSET` should terminate cleanly when the downstream side finishes early instead of throwing a pipeline-stuck exception. Once the output is finished, the transform should close its input and report completion rather than lingering in an invalid state. The desired outcome is that `OFFSET` behaves like a normal pipeline operator under shutdown and short-circuit conditions.

  '

=== old-format-parent-check ===
title: Fix checking parent for old-format parts
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse operator using zero-copy replication with old-format parts needs part cleanup to distinguish real parent-child relationships from cases where no parent lock should be consulted.

  ## Desired outcome

  Parent-part checks during shared-blob unlock should only apply when the part format actually has a parent mutation relationship, so normal cleanup is not blocked or misclassified.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Old-format parts can be cleaned up without spurious parent lookups, while mutated parts still keep any parent blobs that are genuinely shared.

  '

=== old-parts-autoremoval ===
title: Allow autoremoval of old parts if detach_not_byte_identical_parts enabled
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators who enable `detach_not_byte_identical_parts` do so to preserve problematic data for inspection, but they still need stale superseded parts to disappear automatically over time.

  ## Desired outcome

  Old parts that are safe to forget should remain eligible for automatic cleanup even when detached non-byte-identical parts are being kept for diagnostics.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The setting no longer causes obsolete parts to accumulate indefinitely just because a diagnostic detached copy exists.

  '

=== on-cluster-replicated-database ===
title: Fix ON CLUSTER with Replicated database cluster
category: bugfix
requirement: 'A ClickHouse operator using Replicated databases should be able to run ON CLUSTER statements without the clause being stripped too broadly. Queries that are already replicated at the database layer may still ignore ON CLUSTER, but operations such as ALTER ... DROP PARTITION ON CLUSTER need to preserve cluster-wide behavior so partitions are handled correctly across shards and replicas, including ordinary MergeTree and ReplicatedMergeTree tables. The desired outcome is that ON CLUSTER is ignored only where database-level replication truly makes it redundant.

  '

=== opentelemetry-stress-stability ===
title: Fix failed stress test (OpenTelemetry)
category: bugfix
requirement: 'OpenTelemetry context propagation must stay stable under concurrency and exception paths instead of corrupting tracing state during stress workloads. The tracing context code should be exception-safe so failed updates do not leak partial state, and repeated high-volume requests continue producing correct trace relationships rather than intermittently breaking the server-side telemetry path.

  '

=== orc-nested-batch-sizing ===
title: Fix very strange behavior of Apache ORC
category: bugfix
requirement: 'A user exporting data to ORC should get a valid file even when rows contain arrays or maps with nested values. ClickHouse currently mis-sizes ORC batches in some of these cases, which can produce corrupted output or incorrect null bookkeeping. The desired outcome is that ORC export always allocates enough space for both nested elements and per-row null markers so the generated file can be read back correctly by ORC consumers.

  '

=== order-by-desc-limit-flake ===
title: Fix flaky 01926_order_by_desc_limit
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Engineers rely on the regression suite to catch real `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` problems, but a flaky check burns CI time and obscures genuine failures.

  ## Desired outcome

  Stabilize the `01926_order_by_desc_limit` coverage so it still validates the intended descending-order behavior without depending on timing-sensitive log windows.

  ## Acceptance signals

  CI continues to cover the scenario, but the test no longer fails intermittently for reasons unrelated to product behavior.

  '

1	title: PODArray assign empty array fix
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  C++ contributors using `PODArray` and `PaddedPODArray` expect `assign({})` to behave like a normal clear operation, but empty-assignment paths can leave the container in an inconsistent state after previous contents existed.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  Assigning an empty initializer list should leave the array valid and empty regardless of its prior size, inline-storage mode, or subsequent move and swap operations.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals
12	
13	  Both `PODArray` and `PaddedPODArray` stay usable after `assign({})`, report an empty size correctly, and still support later move and swap operations without corruption.
14	
15	  '

1	title: Fix overflow in `PODArray`
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: 'A ClickHouse operator importing external data should not be able to crash the server or trigger integer-overflow behavior just by feeding it corrupt or maliciously large arrays, strings, or schema descriptions. When deserializing oversized Native-format arrays, FixedString values, or related format metadata, ClickHouse should stop the read and fail the query with a normal size-limit exception instead of overflowing an internal buffer or trying to allocate impossible amounts of memory. The goal is to turn this class of malformed-input failures into safe, user-visible errors rather than process instability.
4	
5	  '

1	title: Fix build on master
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Main-branch builds must keep compiling on platforms where the `poll` timeout parameter requires an explicit integer type rather than relying on an implicit conversion from a wider value. A seemingly minor mismatch here can block development even though the resolver logic is correct.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The c-ares PTR resolver should pass its computed timeout to `poll` with an explicit integer conversion so the code builds reliably across toolchains without altering runtime waiting behavior. This is a build-stability fix and should not change DNS lookup semantics.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The resolver code compiles on the affected toolchains, the timeout still represents the same duration at runtime, and users see no behavioral change beyond the restored buildability of the branch.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Fix for positional arguments
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: 'A SQL user who enables positional arguments should be able to write GROUP BY 1, ORDER BY 1, or LIMIT BY positional references without tripping a Positional argument out of bounds error during analysis. With enable_positional_arguments = 1, ordinal references need to be resolved against the select list before normalization so positional arguments and ordinary aliases can coexist correctly in the same query. The desired outcome is that positional clauses behave predictably instead of failing during rewriting.
4	
5	  '

1	title: 'fix(typo): Passible -> Possible'
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Kafka engine users read built-in setting descriptions to learn which option values are supported, and typos in those descriptions create needless uncertainty in documentation and UI surfaces that expose the setting help. This is a wording fix, not a semantic change.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Correct the help text for `kafka_handle_error_mode` so it says "Possible values" instead of the misspelled wording, while keeping the setting name, default, and accepted values unchanged.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Wherever Kafka setting descriptions are surfaced, `kafka_handle_error_mode` now presents a clean description that correctly lists its possible values without changing the engine''s actual behavior.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Fix build after merge
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: 'This is a build-correctness follow-up after a bad merge. The project should compile cleanly again, with no intended change to query behavior, settings semantics, or public interfaces. Users should only notice that the tree is buildable and releasable again.
4	
5	  '

1	title: Fix postgres db engine attaching table with datetime
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A team using the PostgreSQL database engine can successfully work with tables that contain timestamp data, but `ATTACH TABLE` fails for those PostgreSQL-backed tables once datetime columns are present. That makes reconnecting existing tables unreliable.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Attaching an existing PostgreSQL table should work for schemas that include timestamp-based columns, with the same type mapping users already get during normal reads.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A PostgreSQL timestamp column can be attached without error, and the exposed ClickHouse type for that mapping is `DateTime64(6)`.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Improve feedback when replacing partition with different primary key
2	category: ci
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When an operator tries to replace a partition from one MergeTree table into another that does not share the same primary key, the current failure feedback is too vague to explain why the operation was rejected.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Reject this case with a direct, user-facing explanation that the `REPLACE PARTITION` source and destination tables have different primary keys. The operation should fail before any partial replacement work starts.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  An invalid replace-partition attempt now surfaces the explicit message `Tables have different primary key`, making the incompatibility immediately clear to the operator. Successful replacements with matching structure continue to work normally.
16	
17	  '

1	title: 'Play: recognize tab in textarea'
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context

5	  Users editing longer SQL examples in the built-in Playground cannot press Tab inside the textarea to indent their query, because focus moves away instead of treating Tab as editor input.
6	
7	  ## Desired outcome
8	
9	  The Playground editor should recognize Tab inside the textarea so multi-line queries can be formatted naturally in place.
10	
11	  ## Acceptance signals

14	
15	  '

1	title: 'Play UI: add row numbers; add cell selection on click; add hysteresis for table cells.'
2	category: feature
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Users exploring result sets in Play UI need lightweight table interactions that make large outputs easier to inspect visually. Today there is no row-number reference, clicked cells do not remain selected, and hover feedback disappears too abruptly while the pointer is moving across the table.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The result grid should show row numbers when the result is large enough to benefit from them, allow a clicked cell to stay visibly selected, and keep hover highlighting around just long enough to make cross-cell inspection easier.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Result tables with more than a few rows display a `№` column for row numbers, clicking a cell leaves it selected, and the hover state has visible hysteresis instead of vanishing immediately as the pointer moves away.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Fix a few usability issues in Play UI
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context

5	  People using Play UI expect it to feel consistent across devices and across repeated query runs. Right now the page can render with stray browser styling on iPad-like layouts, and the progress indicator can disappear after the first query even though later queries are still running.

7	
8	  ## Desired outcome

10	  Play UI should use a cleaner, more consistent layout baseline and should keep showing progress feedback on every query, not just the first one.

12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals

15	  The interface no longer inherits the unwanted margins and border radii that made it look off on tablet browsers, and the progress indication appears reliably for successive queries instead of only once.
16	
17	  '

1	title: Disable merge tree table with lightweight delete virtual column name _row_exists
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A ClickHouse user working with `*MergeTree` tables can accidentally define a real column called `_row_exists`, even though that name is reserved internally for the lightweight delete feature. This creates a confusing situation where user schema and engine-managed behavior collide, especially during later `ALTER` operations.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  `*MergeTree` engines should treat `_row_exists` as reserved and reject attempts to create a table with that column name, add it later, or rename another column to `_row_exists`. The failure should happen immediately with an `ILLEGAL_COLUMN` error instead of allowing a schema that conflicts with lightweight deletes. This restriction should apply only to the MergeTree family; engines such as `Memory` should keep their existing behavior.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Users cannot create or alter a `*MergeTree` table in a way that introduces `_row_exists` as a regular column, and the rejection clearly explains that the name is reserved for lightweight delete. Existing behavior for non-MergeTree engines remains unchanged.
16	
17	  '

The current queue message says that two log entries for the same part being processed at once `shouldn''t happen often`, which adds unnecessary speculation to an otherwise useful explanation.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The log should explain the conflicting queue entries plainly without the editorial comment. This is a wording cleanup only; replication behavior and scheduling must remain unchanged.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The message still identifies both log entries, their types, and the part involved, but it no longer ends with `This shouldn''t happen often.`.'
