title: Choose correct aggregation method for lc128 and lc256
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user grouping on large integer dimensions stored as `LowCardinality(UInt128)` or `LowCardinality(UInt256)` should get the same reliable aggregation behavior they already get for smaller low-cardinality numeric types.


  ## Desired outcome

  Queries that build aggregation keys from these 128-bit and 256-bit low-cardinality columns should choose the correct aggregation path instead of falling into an invalid method for the column width.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `GROUP BY` and similar aggregation workloads over `LowCardinality(UInt128)` and `LowCardinality(UInt256)` run successfully and return correct results without logical errors or type-selection regressions.

  '
title: Fix missing `metadata_version` for old tables
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Clusters upgrading to newer ClickHouse versions can fail to attach old `ReplicatedMergeTree` tables that were originally created by very old releases and never altered afterward. Those tables may have `/metadata` in ZooKeeper but no replica-local `/metadata_version`, which blocks startup even though the table definition itself is valid.


  ## Desired outcome

  When attaching such legacy replicated tables, ClickHouse should initialize `metadata_version` from the table metadata stored in ZooKeeper if the replica is missing that node. If another server changes the table concurrently, the attach logic should detect that race, report `REPLICA_STATUS_CHANGED`, and retry instead of leaving the table stuck.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Old unaltered replicated tables can start successfully on newer releases without requiring manual ZooKeeper repair. Concurrent metadata changes still trigger a safe retry path rather than silently initializing an incorrect version.

  '
title: Fix usage of generator expressions for libcxx cmake
category: bugfix
requirement: 'A ClickHouse builder should be able to configure the project from a source tree rooted at paths like `/src` without libc++''s CMake generator expressions treating that source directory as an exported include path and failing configuration. The libc++ build glue should keep the source include path private to that dependency so local builds and packaging runs complete cleanly instead of stopping during CMake configure.

  '

title: Prepare library-bridge for catboost integration
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Developers extending `clickhouse-library-bridge` for future CatBoost-based integrations need cleaner internal boundaries before new handlers can be added safely. This preparatory work should make the bridge easier to evolve without changing the behavior users already depend on.


  ## Desired outcome

  The bridge internals should be reorganized to support upcoming CatBoost integration while preserving the current external behavior and protocol seen by existing callers.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The codebase exposes clearer separation for future library-backed handlers, but current bridge requests continue to behave exactly as they did before this preparatory refactor.

  '
title: Further preparation for catboost integration into library-bridge
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Developers preparing library-bridge integrations need a minimal protocol version signal so bridge components can evolve without guesswork. This is groundwork for future integrations and should not disrupt current bridge users.


  ## Desired outcome

  The bridge communication layer should carry a simple explicit version field that future handlers can rely on, while keeping existing request behavior compatible.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Bridge-side code can detect the protocol version through the new field, and current bridge functionality continues to behave the same for existing callers.

  '
title: Document how the library-bridge port can be changed
category: docs
requirement: '## Context

  Users deploying executable UDFs through the library bridge need documentation for moving the bridge off its default port, because network policy and port conflicts are common in production environments.


  ## Desired outcome

  Document how to change the library-bridge port so operators can configure it intentionally instead of reverse-engineering the setup from scattered references.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reader can find clear instructions for changing the library-bridge port and apply them without trial and error.

  '
title: Add llvm-15 for llvm-symbolizer-15 for clang-15 (used for TSan)
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Maintainers debugging ThreadSanitizer failures from clang-15 builds need symbolized stack traces from the packaging image instead of raw addresses.


  ## Desired outcome

  The binary build environment should include the LLVM 15 symbolizer tooling needed by clang-15 and TSan, specifically `llvm-symbolizer-15`, so sanitizer reports are readable during CI and local packaging runs.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The packaging image installs the LLVM 15 symbolizer tooling, clang-15 TSan reports resolve symbols correctly, and the rest of the packaging flow stays unchanged.

  '

4	+++ b/docs/en/sql-reference/statements/alter/projection.md

6	 slug: /en/sql-reference/statements/alter/projection
7	 sidebar_position: 49
8	 sidebar_label: PROJECTION
9	-title: "Manipulating Projections"
10	+title: "Projections"
11	 ---
12	 
13	+Projections store data in a format that optimizes query execution, this feature is useful for:
14	+- Running queries on a column that is not a part of the primary key
15	+- Pre-aggregating columns, it will reduce both computation and IO
16	+
17	+You can define one or more projections for a table, and during the query analysis the projection with the least data to scan will be selected by ClickHouse without modifying the query provided by the user.
18	+
19	+## Example filtering without using primary keys
20	+
21	+Creating the table:
22	+```
23	+CREATE TABLE visits_order
24	+(
25	+   `user_id` UInt64,
26	+   `user_name` String,
27	+   `pages_visited` Nullable(Float64),
28	+   `user_agent` String
29	+)
30	+ENGINE = MergeTree()
31	+PRIMARY KEY user_agent
32	+```
33	+Using `ALTER TABLE`, we could add the Projection to an existing table:
34	+```
35	+ALTER TABLE visits_order ADD PROJECTION user_name_projection (
36	+SELECT
37	+* 
38	+ORDER BY user_name
39	+)
40	+
41	+ALTER TABLE visits_order MATERIALIZE PROJECTION user_name_projection
42	+```
43	+Inserting the data:
44	+```
45	+INSERT INTO visits_order SELECT
46	+    number,
47	+    'test',
48	+    1.5 * (number / 2),
49	+    'Android'
50	+FROM numbers(1, 100);
51	+```
52	+
53	+The Projection will allow us to filter by `user_name` fast even if in the original Table `user_name` was not defined as a `PRIMARY_KEY`.
54	+At query time ClickHouse determined that less data will be processed if the projection is used, as the data is ordered by `user_name`.
55	+```
56	+SELECT
57	+    *
58	+FROM visits_order
59	+WHERE user_name='test'
60	+LIMIT 2
61	+```
62	+
63	+To verify that a query is using the projection, we could review the `system.query_log` table. On the `projections` field we have the name of the projection used or empty if none has been used:
64	+```
65	+SELECT query, projections FROM system.query_log WHERE query_id='<query_id>'
66	+```
67	+
68	+## Example pre-aggregation query
69	+
70	+Creating the table with the Projection:
71	+```
72	+CREATE TABLE visits
73	+(
74	+   `user_id` UInt64,
75	+   `user_name` String,
76	+   `pages_visited` Nullable(Float64),
77	+   `user_agent` String,
78	+   PROJECTION projection_visits_by_user
79	+   (
80	+       SELECT
81	+           user_agent,
82	+           sum(pages_visited)
83	+       GROUP BY user_id, user_agent
84	+   )
85	+)
86	+ENGINE = MergeTree()
87	+ORDER BY user_agent
88	+```
89	+Inserting the data:
90	+```
91	+INSERT INTO visits SELECT
92	+    number,
93	+    'test',
94	+    1.5 * (number / 2),
95	+    'Android'
96	+FROM numbers(1, 100);
97	+```
98	+```
99	+INSERT INTO visits SELECT
100	+    number,
101	+    'test',
102	+    1. * (number / 2),
103	+   'IOS'
104	+FROM numbers(100, 500);
105	+```
106	+We will execute a first query using `GROUP BY` using the field `user_agent`, this query will not use the projection defined as the pre-aggregation does not match.
107	+```
108	+SELECT
109	+    user_agent,
110	+    count(DISTINCT user_id)
111	+FROM visits
112	+GROUP BY user_agent
113	+```
114	+
115	+To use the projection we could execute queries that select part of, or all of the pre-aggregation and `GROUP BY` fields.
116	+```
117	+SELECT
118	+    user_agent
119	+FROM visits
120	+WHERE user_id > 50 AND user_id < 150
121	+GROUP BY user_agent
122	+```
123	+```
124	+SELECT
125	+    user_agent,
126	+    sum(pages_visited)
127	+FROM visits
128	+GROUP BY user_id
129	+```
130	+
131	+As mentioned before, we could review the `system.query_log` table. On the `projections` field we have the name of the projection used or empty if none has been used:
132	+```
133	+SELECT query, projections FROM system.query_log WHERE query_id='<query_id>'
134	+```
135	+

99	    const Names & column_names,
100	    const StorageSnapshotPtr & storage_snapshot,
101	    SelectQueryInfo & query_info,
102	    ContextPtr context,
103	    QueryProcessingStage::Enum processed_stage,
104	    size_t /*max_block_size*/,

110	
111	    auto iterator = std::make_shared<StorageS3Source::DisclosedGlobIterator>(
112	        *s3_configuration.client, s3_configuration.uri, query_info.query, virtual_block, context);
113	    auto callback = std::make_shared<StorageS3Source::IteratorWrapper>([iterator]() mutable -> String { return iterator->next(); });
114

116	    Block header =

118

120

124

139	            /// For unknown reason global context is passed to IStorage::read() method

141	            auto remote_query_executor = std::make_shared<RemoteQueryExecutor>(
142	                connection,
143	                queryToString(query_info.original_query),
144	                header,

38	void TableFunctionS3Cluster::parseArguments(const ASTPtr & ast_function, ContextPtr context)
39	{
40	    /// Parse args
41	    ASTs & args_func = ast_function->children;
42	
43	    if (args_func.size() != 1)
44	        throw Exception("Table function '" + getName() + "' must have arguments.", ErrorCodes::NUMBER_OF_ARGUMENTS_DOESNT_MATCH);
45	
46	    ASTs & args = args_func.at(0)->children;
47	
48	    for (auto & arg : args)
49	        arg = evaluateConstantExpressionAsLiteral(arg, context);
50	
51	    const auto message = fmt::format(
52	        "The signature of table function {} could be the following:\n" \
53	        " - cluster, url\n"
54	        " - cluster, url, format\n" \
55	        " - cluster, url, format, structure\n" \
56	        " - cluster, url, access_key_id, secret_access_key\n" \
57	        " - cluster, url, format, structure, compression_method\n" \
58	        " - cluster, url, access_key_id, secret_access_key, format\n"
59	        " - cluster, url, access_key_id, secret_access_key, format, structure\n" \
60	        " - cluster, url, access_key_id, secret_access_key, format, structure, compression_method",
61	        getName());
62	
63	    if (args.size() < 2 || args.size() > 7)
64	        throw Exception(message, ErrorCodes::NUMBER_OF_ARGUMENTS_DOESNT_MATCH);
65	
66	    /// This arguments are always the first
67	    configuration.cluster_name = checkAndGetLiteralArgument<String>(args[0], "cluster_name");
68	
69	    if (!context->tryGetCluster(configuration.cluster_name))
70	        throw Exception(ErrorCodes::BAD_GET, "Requested cluster '{}' not found", configuration.cluster_name);
71	
72	    /// Just cut the first arg (cluster_name) and try to parse s3 table function arguments as is
73	    ASTs clipped_args;
74	    clipped_args.reserve(args.size());
75	    std::copy(args.begin() + 1, args.end(), std::back_inserter(clipped_args));
76	
77	    /// StorageS3ClusterConfiguration inherints from StorageS3Configuration, so it is safe to upcast it.
78	    TableFunctionS3::parseArgumentsImpl(message, clipped_args, context, static_cast<StorageS3Configuration & >(configuration));
79	}

82	ColumnsDescription TableFunctionS3Cluster::getActualTableStructure(ContextPtr context) const
83	{
84	    if (configuration.structure == "auto")
85	    {
86	        return StorageS3::getTableStructureFromData(
87	            configuration.format,
88	            S3::URI(Poco::URI(configuration.url)),
89	            configuration.auth_settings.access_key_id,
90	            configuration.auth_settings.secret_access_key,
91	            configuration.compression_method,
92	            false,
93	            std::nullopt,
94	            context);
95	    }
96	
97	    return parseColumnsListFromString(configuration.structure, context);
98	}
99	
100	StoragePtr TableFunctionS3Cluster::executeImpl(
101	    const ASTPtr & /*function*/, ContextPtr context,
102	    const std::string & table_name, ColumnsDescription /*cached_columns*/) const
103	{
104	    StoragePtr storage;
105	
106	    ColumnsDescription columns;
107	    if (configuration.structure != "auto")
108	        columns = parseColumnsListFromString(configuration.structure, context);
109	    else if (!structure_hint.empty())
110	        columns = structure_hint;
111	
112	    if (context->getClientInfo().query_kind == ClientInfo::QueryKind::SECONDARY_QUERY)
113	    {
114	        /// On worker node this filename won't contains globs
115	        Poco::URI uri (configuration.url);
116	        S3::URI s3_uri (uri);
117	        storage = std::make_shared<StorageS3>(
118	            s3_uri,
119	            configuration.auth_settings.access_key_id,
120	            configuration.auth_settings.secret_access_key,
121	            StorageID(getDatabaseName(), table_name),
122	            configuration.format,
123	            configuration.rw_settings,
124	            columns,
125	            ConstraintsDescription{},
126	            String{},
127	            context,
128	            // No format_settings for S3Cluster
129	            std::nullopt,
130	            configuration.compression_method,
131	            /*distributed_processing=*/true);
132	    }
133	    else
134	    {
135	        storage = std::make_shared<StorageS3Cluster>(
136	            configuration.url,
137	            configuration.auth_settings.access_key_id,
138	            configuration.auth_settings.secret_access_key,
139	            StorageID(getDatabaseName(), table_name),
140	            configuration.cluster_name, configuration.format,
141	            columns,
142	            ConstraintsDescription{},
143	            context,
144	            configuration.compression_method);
145	    }
146	
147	    storage->startup();
148	
149	    return storage;
150	}

        "message": "Fix a spurious AST fuzzer abort on a recycled node address\n\n`QueryFuzzer::fuzz` detects loops in the AST by remembering the address of every\nnode it visits during one `fuzzMain` call, and calls `std::abort` when it sees an\naddress twice. But fuzzing legitimately destroys parts of the query it has\nalready visited: wrapping a table into `Remote` / `Distributed` / `Buffer` drops\nthe whole column list, a random constraint or projection is erased, a key clause\nis removed from a storage definition, a child is replaced with a new node. Once\nsuch a node is freed, the allocator is free to hand its address to a node created\nlater - for instance to a data type parsed by `fuzzColumnDeclaration` for a\ncolumn of another table - and the check then aborts the server although the AST\ncontains no loop at all.\n\nThis is what happened in the report below, where the fuzzer wrapped\n`CREATE TABLE table1(x Int32)` into `Remote(...)` (dropping the already visited\ncolumn list of `table1`) and then parsed `Array(UInt16)` for the column of\n`table2`: the dumped AST contains the reported node exactly once.\n\nKeep every visited node alive for the duration of the `fuzzMain` call, so that\nits address cannot be recycled and pointer identity remains a valid answer to\n\"have I visited this node before\".\n\nhttps://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=dd1e53dfe2715c22d4b7e63c2459bc9eec994581&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29",

31	A tool to extract information from Git repository for analytics.
32	
33	It dumps the data for the following tables:
34	- commits - commits with statistics;
35	- file_changes - files changed in every commit with the info about the change and statistics;
36	- line_changes - every changed line in every changed file in every commit with full info about the line and the information about previous change of this line.
37	
38	The largest and the most important table is "line_changes".
39	
40	Allows to answer questions like:
41	- list files with maximum number of authors;
42	- show me the oldest lines of code in the repository;
43	- show me the files with longest history;
44	- list favorite files for author;
45	- list largest files with lowest number of authors;
46	- at what weekday the code has highest chance to stay in repository;
47	- the distribution of code age across repository;
48	- files sorted by average code age;
49	- quickly show file with blame info (rough);
50	- commits and lines of code distribution by time; by weekday, by author; for specific subdirectories;
51	- show history for every subdirectory, file, line of file, the number of changes (lines and commits) across time; how the number of contributors was changed across time;
52	- list files with most modifications;
53	- list files that were rewritten most number of time or by most of authors;
54	- what is percentage of code removal by other authors, across authors;
55	- the matrix of authors that shows what authors tends to rewrite another authors code;
56	- what is the worst time to write code in sense that the code has highest chance to be rewritten;
57	- the average time before code will be rewritten and the median (half-life of code decay);
58	- comments/code percentage change in time / by author / by location;
59	- who tend to write more tests / cpp code / comments.
60	
61	The data is intended for analytical purposes. It can be imprecise by many reasons but it should be good enough for its purpose.
62	
63	The data is not intended to provide any conclusions for managers, it is especially counter-indicative for any kinds of "performance review". Instead you can spend multiple days looking at various interesting statistics.
64	
65	Run this tool inside your git repository. It will create .tsv files that can be loaded into ClickHouse (or into other DBMS if you dare).
66

---
sidebar_position: 1
sidebar_label: 英国房价数据集
---

# 英国房价数据集（UK Property Price Paid）

本数据集包含自 1995 年以来英格兰和威尔士地区不动产交易的价格信息。数据来源于英国皇家土地注册处（HM Land Registry）公开的 *Price Paid Data*，包含约 2700 万条记录，是学习 ClickHouse 分析能力的绝佳示例。

在本教程中，你将完成以下步骤：

1. 创建用于存放数据集的表；
2. 将数据下载并加载到 ClickHouse 中；
3. 运行校验查询确认数据加载正确；
4. 运行示例分析查询；
5. 使用物化投影（projection）加速查询。

## 1. 创建表 {#create-table}

数据集中的每一条记录描述一次房产交易。我们使用如下 `MergeTree` 表来存储它：

```sql
CREATE TABLE uk_price_paid
(
    price UInt32,
    date Date,
    postcode1 LowCardinality(String),
    postcode2 LowCardinality(String),
    type Enum8('terraced' = 1, 'semi-detached' = 2, 'detached' = 3, 'flat' = 4, 'other' = 0),
    is_new UInt8,
    duration Enum8('freehold' = 1, 'leasehold' = 2, 'unknown' = 0),
    addr1 String,
    addr2 String,
    street LowCardinality(String),
    locality LowCardinality(String),
    town LowCardinality(String),
    district LowCardinality(String),
    county LowCardinality(String),
    category UInt8
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY (postcode1, postcode2, addr1, addr2);
```

字段说明：

- `price`：成交价格（英镑）；
- `date`：成交日期；
- `postcode1` / `postcode2`：英国邮编的两部分；
- `type`：房产类型（联排、半独栋、独栋、公寓等）；
- `is_new`：是否新建房产；
- `duration`：产权类型（永久产权 freehold / 租赁产权 leasehold）；
- `addr1`、`addr2`、`street`、`locality`、`town`、`district`、`county`：地址各层级；
- `category`：交易类别。

## 2. 下载并加载数据 {#load-data}

完整数据可以从英国皇家土地注册处下载为单个 CSV 文件（约 4 GB）。借助 `clickhouse-local`，我们可以在下载的同时直接将数据流式写入表：

```bash
wget -O- http://prod.publicdata.landregistry.gov.uk.s3-website-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/pp-complete.csv \
  | clickhouse-local \
      --input-format CSV \
      --structure "
        uuid String,
        price UInt32,
        time DateTime,
        postcode String,
        a String,
        b String,
        c String,
        addr1 String,
        addr2 String,
        street String,
        locality String,
        town String,
        district String,
        county String,
        d String,
        e String" \
      --query "
        WITH splitByChar(' ', postcode) AS p
        INSERT INTO uk_price_paid
        SELECT
            price,
            toDate(time) AS date,
            p[1] AS postcode1,
            p[2] AS postcode2,
            transform(a, ['terraced', 'semi-detached', 'detached', 'flat'], [1, 2, 3, 4], 0)::UInt8 AS type,
            b = 'Y' AS is_new,
            transform(c, ['F', 'L'], [1, 2], 0)::UInt8 AS duration,
            addr1, addr2, street, locality, town, district, county,
            d = 'A' AS category"
```

说明：

- 下载可能需要几分钟到几十分钟，取决于网络状况；
- `splitByChar` 用于把邮编拆成两部分；
- `transform` 把文本枚举值映射为数值。

## 3. 校验数据 {#validate}

加载完成后，先确认行数：

```sql
SELECT count() FROM uk_price_paid;
```

```text
┌──count()─┐
│ 27643249 │
└──────────┘
```

再看几条样例数据：

```sql
SELECT * FROM uk_price_paid LIMIT 3;
```

## 4. 示例分析查询 {#example-queries}

### 各年份平均房价 {#avg-price-per-year}

```sql
SELECT
    toYear(date) AS year,
    round(avg(price)) AS price,
    bar(price, 0, 1000000, 80)
FROM uk_price_paid
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year;
```

可以看到 1995 年至今英国平均房价的走势，以及 2008 年金融危机前后的变化。

### 各城镇平均房价 {#avg-price-per-town}

```sql
SELECT
    town,
    round(avg(price)) AS price,
    bar(price, 0, 2000000, 100)
FROM uk_price_paid
GROUP BY town
ORDER BY price DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### 伦敦最贵街区 {#most-expensive-areas-in-london}

```sql
SELECT
    county,
    round(avg(price)) AS price
FROM uk_price_paid
WHERE county LIKE '%LONDON%'
GROUP BY county
ORDER BY price DESC;
```

### 条件聚合 {#conditional-aggregation}

比较新建房与二手房的均价：

```sql
SELECT
    toYear(date) AS year,
    round(avgIf(price, is_new = 1)) AS new_price,
    round(avgIf(price, is_new = 0)) AS old_price
FROM uk_price_paid
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year;
```

## 5. 使用投影加速查询 {#projections}

从 22.6 版本开始，ClickHouse 支持物化投影（projection），可以为常用聚合预先计算结果，从而显著加速查询。

以“各年份平均房价”为例，先添加一个投影：

```sql
ALTER TABLE uk_price_paid
    ADD PROJECTION projection_by_year
    (
        SELECT toYear(date), avg(price)
        GROUP BY toYear(date)
    );

ALTER TABLE uk_price_paid
    MATERIALIZE PROJECTION projection_by_year
    SETTINGS mutations_sync = 1;
```

再次运行同样的查询：

```sql
SELECT
    toYear(date) AS year,
    round(avg(price)) AS price
FROM uk_price_paid
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year;
```

启用投影后，ClickHouse 会直接读取预聚合的数据，无需扫描全部 2700 万行，查询耗时通常可以从秒级降到毫秒级。可以通过查询日志中的 `selected_projections` 字段，或用 `EXPLAIN` 语句确认投影是否被命中：

```sql
EXPLAIN indexes = 1
SELECT toYear(date), avg(price)
FROM uk_price_paid
GROUP BY toYear(date);
```

## 小结 {#summary}

本教程演示了完整的数据分析流程：创建表、加载公开数据集、校验数据、执行分析查询，以及通过投影进行性能优化。你可以在自己的 ClickHouse 实例上复现全部步骤，并尝试更多查询。

**数据集大小**：约 2700 万行
**原始数据**：[HM Land Registry Price Paid Data](http://prod.publicdata.landregistry.gov.uk.s3-website-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/pp-complete.csv)

# 英国房价数据集（UK Property Price Paid）

本数据集包含自 1995 年以来英格兰和威尔士地区不动产交易的价格信息。数据来源于英国皇家土地注册处（HM Land Registry）公开的 *Price Paid Data*，包含约 2700 万条记录，是学习 ClickHouse 分析能力的绝佳示例。

在本教程中，你将完成以下步骤：

1. 创建用于存放数据集的表；
2. 将数据下载并加载到 ClickHouse 中；
3. 运行校验查询确认数据加载正确；

```sql
CREATE TABLE uk_price_paid
(
    price UInt32,
    date Date,
    postcode1 LowCardinality(String),
    postcode2 LowCardinality(String),
    type Enum8('terraced' = 1, 'semi-detached' = 2, 'detached' = 3, 'flat' = 4, 'other' = 0),
    is_new UInt8,
    duration Enum8('freehold' = 1, 'leasehold' = 2, 'unknown' = 0),
    addr1 String,
    addr2 String,
    street LowCardinality(String),
    locality LowCardinality(String),
    town LowCardinality(String),
    district LowCardinality(String),
    county LowCardinality(String),
    category UInt8
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
ORDER BY (postcode1, postcode2, addr1, addr2);
```

- `date`：成交日期；
- `postcode1` / `postcode2`：英国邮编的两部分；
- `type`：房产类型（联排、半独栋、独栋、公寓等）；

requirements/profile-events-tracing.yaml:5:  A ClickHouse operator who enables `trace_profile_events` to diagnose slow or unstable queries needs tracing to stay informative without creating feedback loops inside the tracing machinery itself. Right now some internal profile events generated while profiling or handling failed writes can recursively enter the trace log again, which makes stress runs noisy and can destabilize the very diagnostics people turned on.
requirements/profile-events-tracing.yaml:10:  Tracing should still report normal query-level profile events, but internal bookkeeping events such as `QueryProfilerSignalOverruns` and write failures that are counted only for observability must be recorded without sending those same counters back into the trace log. In other words, operators should be able to leave `trace_profile_events` enabled during heavy profiling and failed-write scenarios without seeing self-generated trace spam or re-entrant logging side effects.
requirements/profile-events-tracing.yaml:15:  A long-running query with `trace_profile_events = 1` still completes and produces trace data, while the internal counters that track profiler overruns or discard-on-failure writes are incremented through the non-tracing path instead of being re-emitted into the trace log. The public contract should make that distinction explicit by using `incrementNoTrace` for events that must never recurse into tracing.'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tags: disabled

CURDIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
# shellcheck source=../shell_config.sh
. "$CURDIR"/../shell_config.sh

$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS parsing_bson"
$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "CREATE TABLE parsing_bson(WatchID UInt64, ClientIP6 FixedString(16), EventTime DateTime, Title String) ENGINE=Memory()"


$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --max_threads=0 --max_block_size=65505 --output_format_parallel_formatting=false -q \
"SELECT WatchID, ClientIP6, EventTime, Title FROM test.hits ORDER BY UserID LIMIT 100000 Format BSONEachRow" > 00176_data.bson

cat 00176_data.bson | $CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --max_threads=0 --max_block_size=65505 --input_format_parallel_parsing=false -q "INSERT INTO parsing_bson FORMAT BSONEachRow"

checksum1=$($CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "SELECT * FROM parsing_bson ORDER BY WatchID;" | md5sum)
$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "TRUNCATE TABLE parsing_bson;"

cat 00176_data.bson | $CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --max_threads=0 --max_block_size=65505 --input_format_parallel_parsing=true -q "INSERT INTO parsing_bson FORMAT BSONEachRow"

checksum2=$($CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "SELECT * FROM parsing_bson ORDER BY WatchID;" | md5sum)


if [[ "$checksum1" == "$checksum2" ]];
then
    echo "OK"
else
    echo "FAIL"
fi

$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "DROP TABLE parsing_bson"

rm 00176_data.bson

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tags: disabled

CURDIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
# shellcheck source=../shell_config.sh
. "$CURDIR"/../shell_config.sh

$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS parsing_bson"
$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "CREATE TABLE parsing_bson(WatchID UInt64, ClientIP6 FixedString(16), EventTime DateTime, Title String) ENGINE=Memory()"


$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --max_threads=0 --max_block_size=65505 --output_format_parallel_formatting=false -q \
"SELECT WatchID, ClientIP6, EventTime, Title FROM test.hits ORDER BY UserID LIMIT 100000 Format BSONEachRow" > 00176_data.bson

cat 00176_data.bson | $CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --max_threads=0 --max_block_size=65505 --input_format_parallel_parsing=false -q "INSERT INTO parsing_bson FORMAT BSONEachRow"

checksum1=$($CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "SELECT * FROM parsing_bson ORDER BY WatchID;" | md5sum)
$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "TRUNCATE TABLE parsing_bson;"

cat 00176_data.bson | $CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --max_threads=0 --max_block_size=65505 --input_format_parallel_parsing=true -q "INSERT INTO parsing_bson FORMAT BSONEachRow"

checksum2=$($CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "SELECT * FROM parsing_bson ORDER BY WatchID;" | md5sum)


if [[ "$checksum1" == "$checksum2" ]];
then
    echo "OK"
else
    echo "FAIL"
fi

$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "DROP TABLE parsing_bson"

rm 00176_data.bson

      "sha": "20dea4f5e66f9829e32a856802e9f3a2100b7632",
        "message": "Isolate 00180_no_seek_avoiding_when_reading_from_cache from other cache users

The test asserts that its measured query reads entirely from the filesystem
cache, but the table is created with `CREATE TABLE hits_s3_sampled AS
test.hits_s3`, so it inherits `storage_policy = 's3_cache'`: the single 200 MiB
cache shared by everything on the server. Background merges of `test.hits_s3`
write through that cache and can fill it with file segments held open by a
`FileSegmentsHolder`, which are not releasable. The warm-up queries' space
reservation then finds nothing to evict, silently continues without caching, and
the measured query reads from S3, so `CachedReadBufferReadFromSourceBytes` is
non-zero. `SYSTEM CLEAR FILESYSTEM CACHE` does not help, since it is
`removeAllReleasable` and skips held segments.

Give the table a private inline cache disk instead, keyed on
`$CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE` so the disk name is unique per run and the test stays
parallel-safe, and scope the cache clear to that cache. The assertion, the
reference file and the tags are unchanged.

`04695_filesystem_cache_wait_for_concurrent_download_timeout.sh` was isolated
the same way in eca7e2270696c02 for this same mechanism.

The explicit `ENGINE = MergeTree` is required. Without it, `setEngine` calls
`inheritStorageFromSource`, whose `mergeStorageSettings` appends the source's
`storage_policy` next to the new `disk` setting, and `loadFromQuery` then throws
`storage_policy and disk cannot be specified at the same time`. With the engine
given explicitly that path is skipped, while columns and the PARTITION BY /
ORDER BY / SAMPLE BY clauses are still copied from the source table.

Validated by reproducing the failure mode locally with a concurrent workload
that keeps the shared cache full of held segments, confirmed by a global cache
clear leaving 229.68 MiB across 46 segments resident. Runs of the real test file
under that workload: 2 of 20 pass[...truncated]

From: Alexey Milovidov <milovidov@clickhouse.com>

Subject: [PATCH] A workaround for LLVM bug,
 https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/58633

---
 cmake/sanitize.cmake | 4 +++-
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/cmake/sanitize.cmake b/cmake/sanitize.cmake

--- a/cmake/sanitize.cmake

 if (SANITIZE)
     if (SANITIZE STREQUAL "address")
-        set (ASAN_FLAGS "-fsanitize=address -fsanitize-address-use-after-scope")
+        # LLVM-15 has a bug in Address Sanitizer, preventing the usage of 'sanitize-address-use-after-scope',

+        set (ASAN_FLAGS "-fsanitize=address -fno-sanitize-address-use-after-scope")

         set (CMAKE_C_FLAGS "${CMAKE_C_FLAGS} ${SAN_FLAGS} ${ASAN_FLAGS}")

Subject: [PATCH] ci: add symlink for llvm-symbolizer (to make symbolizer work)

Simply installing llvm-symbolizer-$VER is not enough, since it does not

 docker/packager/binary/Dockerfile | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

index ba0a27c9801f..b9b0c5c2c6cb 100644

@@ -83,5 +83,8 @@ RUN export CODENAME="$(lsb_release --codename --short | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" \

"message": "Add missing settings in schema inference cache",
        "message": "Add missing top-level config keys consumed outside `ServerSettings` to the allowlist

The review found five top-level server config keys that are read directly
by C++ code (not via `ServerSettings`) and were missing from
`known_complex_sections`, so existing valid configs using them would be
rejected with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG`: `proto_caps` (`TCPHandler`),
`enable_http_close_session` (`HTTPHandler`), `enable_arrow_close_session`
(`ArrowFlight::AuthMiddleware`), `ignore_table_dependencies_on_metadata_loading`
(`TablesLoader`), and `allow_reserved_database_name_tmp_convert`
(`loadMetadata`).

A systematic sweep of the codebase for direct server-config reads found
more keys with the same problem, now also added: `nats`, `azure`,
`iceberg_biglake_metadata_service_hosts` (used by an existing integration
test config), `library_bridge`, `odbc_bridge`, `jdbc_bridge`,
`keeper_map_keys_limit`, `user_defined_path`, `workload_path`,
`resource_overload_warnings`, `distributed_ddl_keeper_max_retries`,
`distributed_ddl_keeper_initial_backoff_ms`,
`distributed_ddl_keeper_max_backoff_ms`,
`schema_inference_cache_max_elements_for_hdfs`,
`schema_inference_cache_max_elements_for_local`, the daemon-level
`umask`, `pid`, `pending_signals` (read by `BaseDaemon`), and
`hsts_max_age` (documented as a top-level server parameter). Per-user
HDFS client sections (`hdfs_USERNAME` with an arbitrary user name) are
covered by a new `hdfs` entry in `known_prefixes`.

Add a positive regression test case `existing_keys` to
`test_unknown_config_option` with a config exercising these keys, so
future allowlist edits cannot silently break them again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>",
        "message": "Address review: add `max_parser_depth` to the ORC schema-inference cache key

`max_parser_depth` bounds the nesting depth in `parseORCType` during schema
inference (throwing `TOO_DEEP_RECURSION` when exceeded), so it changes the
result of `NativeORCSchemaReader::readSchema` and must be part of the schema
cache key. Otherwise a query could cache a deeply nested ORC schema and a later
query with a lower limit would reuse it instead of throwing.

Add a regression test that reproduces the cache poisoning on the unfixed
binary.

        "message": "Address review: prefer literal-filename matches, use the stem only as a fallback

The extensionless stem was OR-ed with the literal filename for every
fixture, so a short or cross-extension stem could pull unrelated prefix
siblings into mappings that the literal filename already resolved
precisely: `format_schemas/03250.proto` gained
`03250_avoid_prefetch_empty_parts` (its bare stem `03250` appears in
that test's table names), and `data_minio/03036_archive1.tar` gained
`03036_schema_inference_cache_s3_archives` (which reads only
`03036_archive1.zip`).

Now candidates matching the literal filename win outright; the stem is
consulted only when no candidate references the full filename, which is
exactly the format-schema convention this PR exists to handle
(`format_schema = 'NNNNN_foo:Message'` for `format_schemas/NNNNN_foo.proto`).
Both tiers remain narrower than the all-prefix-siblings fallback.

        "message": "Fix flacky schema inference cache tests",
        "message": "Fix schema inference for `.jsonl` files broken by the `JSONL` output alias

The previous commit registered `JSONL` as an output format. `FormatFactory::registerOutputFormat` auto-registers a file extension equal to the lower-cased format name, so this re-pointed the `jsonl` file extension from `JSONEachRow` to `JSONL`, undoing the explicit `jsonl` -> `JSONEachRow` mapping set in `registerInputFormatJSONEachRow` (the output registration runs after the input one). - Re-assert the `jsonl` -> `JSONEachRow` extension mapping at the end of `registerOutputFormatJSONEachRow` (which runs after the input registration), so files with a `.jsonl` extension are still resolved to the canonical `JSONEachRow` format, matching the existing `02375_system_schema_inference_cache` reference.

        "message": "Include skip_columns_with_unsupported_types in the ORC schema cache key

`NativeORCSchemaReader::readSchema` uses
`input_format_orc_skip_columns_with_unsupported_types_in_schema_inference`
to decide whether an unsupported ORC column (e.g. a `UNION`) is dropped or
the file is rejected with `UNKNOWN_TYPE`. That setting was missing from the

`registerAdditionalInfoForSchemaCacheGetter` for the `ORC` format, so a query

"skipped" schema instead of throwing.

includes its analogous `skip_columns_with_unsupported_types` flag.

Add regression test `04514_orc_schema_cache_skip_unsupported_types` on an ORC
file with an unsupported `UNION` column: it first infers the schema with the
setting enabled (caching the reduced schema) and then infers it again with
default settings in the same process, asserting the second query re-infers and
throws `UNKNOWN_TYPE` rather than reusing the cached schema.

NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp.

# CREATE FUNCTION — user defined function (UDF)

Creates a user defined function from a lambda expression. The expression must consist of function parameters, constants, operators, or other function calls.

**Syntax**

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION name [ON CLUSTER cluster] AS (parameter0, ...) -> expression;
```

A function can have an arbitrary number of parameters.

There are a few restrictions:

- The name of a function must be unique among user defined and system functions.
- Recursive functions are not allowed.
- All variables used by a function must be specified in its parameter list.

If any restriction is violated then an exception is raised.

**Example**

Query:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION linear_equation AS (x, k, b) -> k * x + b;
SELECT number, linear_equation(number, 2, 1) FROM numbers(3);
```

Result:

```text
┌─number─┬─linear_equation(number, 2, 1)─┐
│      0 │                             1 │
│      1 │                             3 │
│      2 │                             5 │
└────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
```

A conditional function is called in a user defined function as follows:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION parity_str AS (n) -> if(n % 2, 'odd', 'even');
SELECT number, parity_str(number) FROM numbers(3);
```

Result:

```text
┌─number─┬─parity_str(number)─┐
│      0 │ even               │
│      1 │ odd                │
│      2 │ even               │
└────────┴────────────────────┘
```

212	macro(clickhouse_program_add_library name)
213	    string(TOUPPER ${name} name_uc)
214	    string(REPLACE "-" "_" name_uc ${name_uc})
215	
216	    # Some dark magic
217	    set(CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_SOURCES ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_SOURCES} PARENT_SCOPE)
218	    set(CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_LINK ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_LINK} PARENT_SCOPE)
219	    set(CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_INCLUDE ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_INCLUDE} PARENT_SCOPE)
220	
221	    if(NOT CLICKHOUSE_ONE_SHARED)
222	        add_library(clickhouse-${name}-lib ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_SOURCES})
223	
224	        set(_link ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_LINK}) # can't use ${} in if()
225	        if(_link)
226	            target_link_libraries(clickhouse-${name}-lib ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_LINK})
227	        endif()
228	
229	        set(_include ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_INCLUDE}) # can't use ${} in if()
230	        if (_include)
231	            target_include_directories(clickhouse-${name}-lib ${CLICKHOUSE_${name_uc}_INCLUDE})
232	        endif()
233	    endif()
234	endmacro()

242	endmacro()

args.content:
# Analyzing Git Repositories with ClickHouse

This dataset contains the full history of a Git repository (for example, the
[ClickHouse repository on GitHub](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse))
converted into analytical tables by the `clickhouse-git-import` tool. It
allows you to answer questions like:

- list files with maximum number of authors;
- show the oldest lines of code in the repository;
- show the files with the longest history;
- list favorite files for an author;
- commits and lines of code distribution by time, by weekday, by author;
- the distribution of code age across the repository;
- the matrix of authors that shows which authors tend to rewrite another author's code;
- the average time before code will be rewritten (the half-life of code decay);
- comments/code percentage change in time, by author, by location.

## Generating the Data

Build the tool (the source is in `programs/git-import`) and run it inside a
clone of the Git repository you want to analyze:

``` bash
clickhouse-git-import
```

It creates three files in the current directory:

- `commits.tsv` — commits with statistics;
- `file_changes.tsv` — files changed in every commit with statistics;
- `line_changes.tsv` — every changed line in every changed file in every
  commit, with full info about the line and about the previous change of this
  line (rough blame information).

## Creating the Tables

``` sql
CREATE DATABASE git;

CREATE TABLE git.commits
(
    hash String,
    author LowCardinality(String),
    time DateTime,
    message String,
    files_added UInt32,
    files_deleted UInt32,
    files_renamed UInt32,
    files_modified UInt32,
    lines_added UInt32,
    lines_deleted UInt32,
    hunks_added UInt32,
    hunks_removed UInt32,
    hunks_changed UInt32
) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY time;

CREATE TABLE git.file_changes
(
    change_type Enum('Add' = 1, 'Delete' = 2, 'Modify' = 3, 'Rename' = 4, 'Copy' = 5, 'Type' = 6),
    path LowCardinality(String),
    old_path LowCardinality(String),
    file_extension LowCardinality(String),
    lines_added UInt32,
    lines_deleted UInt32,
    hunks_added UInt32,
    hunks_removed UInt32,
    hunks_changed UInt32,

    commit_hash String,
    author LowCardinality(String),
    time DateTime,
    commit_message String,
    commit_files_added UInt32,
    commit_files_deleted UInt32,
    commit_files_renamed UInt32,
    commit_files_modified UInt32,
    commit_lines_added UInt32,
    commit_lines_deleted UInt32,
    commit_hunks_added UInt32,
    commit_hunks_removed UInt32,
    commit_hunks_changed UInt32
) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY time;

CREATE TABLE git.line_changes
(
    sign Int8,
    line_number_old UInt32,
    line_number_new UInt32,
    hunk_num UInt32,
    hunk_start_line_number_old UInt32,
    hunk_start_line_number_new UInt32,
    hunk_lines_added UInt32,
    hunk_lines_deleted UInt32,
    hunk_context LowCardinality(String),
    line LowCardinality(String),
    indent UInt8,
    line_type Enum('Empty' = 0, 'Comment' = 1, 'Punct' = 2, 'Code' = 3),

    prev_commit_hash String,
    prev_author LowCardinality(String),
    prev_time DateTime,

    file_change_type Enum('Add' = 1, 'Delete' = 2, 'Modify' = 3, 'Rename' = 4, 'Copy' = 5, 'Type' = 6),
    path LowCardinality(String),
    old_path LowCardinality(String),
    file_extension LowCardinality(String),
    file_lines_added UInt32,
    file_lines_deleted UInt32,
    file_hunks_added UInt32,
    file_hunks_removed UInt32,
    file_hunks_changed UInt32,

    commit_hash String,
    author LowCardinality(String),
    time DateTime,
    commit_message String,
    commit_files_added UInt32,
    commit_files_deleted UInt32,
    commit_files_renamed UInt32,
    commit_files_modified UInt32,
    commit_lines_added UInt32,
    commit_lines_deleted UInt32,
    commit_hunks_added UInt32,
    commit_hunks_removed UInt32,
    commit_hunks_changed UInt32
) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY time;
```

## Inserting the Data

``` bash
clickhouse-client --query "INSERT INTO git.commits FORMAT TSV" < commits.tsv
clickhouse-client --query "INSERT INTO git.file_changes FORMAT TSV" < file_changes.tsv
clickhouse-client --query "INSERT INTO git.line_changes FORMAT TSV" < line_changes.tsv
```

## Example Queries

### Commits per Month

``` sql
SELECT
    toYYYYMM(time) AS month,
    count() AS commits,
    uniq(author) AS authors
FROM git.commits
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
```

### Lines of Code over Time

``` sql
SELECT
    toYYYYMM(time) AS month,
    sum(commit_lines_added) AS lines_added,
    sum(commit_lines_deleted) AS lines_deleted,
    lines_added - lines_deleted AS net_lines
FROM git.commits
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
```

### Top Authors

``` sql
SELECT
    author,
    count() AS commits,
    sum(lines_added) AS lines_added,
    sum(lines_deleted) AS lines_deleted
FROM git.commits
GROUP BY author
ORDER BY commits DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Files with the Most Authors

``` sql
SELECT
    path,
    uniq(author) AS authors,
    count() AS changes
FROM git.file_changes
GROUP BY path
ORDER BY authors DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### The Oldest Lines of Code

Rough blame information is available in `git.line_changes` through the
`prev_commit_hash`, `prev_author` and `prev_time` columns — for every line
they describe the previous change of that line. To find the lines that
survived the longest:

``` sql
SELECT
    path,
    line_number_new,
    line,
    prev_author,
    prev_time,
    now() - prev_time AS age
FROM git.line_changes
WHERE (sign = 1) AND (line_type = 'Code')
ORDER BY prev_time ASC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Comments to Code Ratio by Author

``` sql
SELECT
    author,
    countIf(line_type = 'Comment') AS comments,
    countIf(line_type = 'Code') AS code,
    comments / code AS comments_to_code_ratio
FROM git.line_changes
WHERE sign = 1
GROUP BY author
HAVING code > 1000
ORDER BY comments_to_code_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Average Indentation by File Extension

The `indent` column contains the number of leading whitespaces of a line
(tabs are counted as 4 spaces), so you can compare coding styles:

``` sql
SELECT
    file_extension,
    avg(indent) AS avg_indent,
    quantile(0.9)(indent) AS p90_indent
FROM git.line_changes
WHERE (sign = 1) AND (line_type = 'Code')
GROUP BY file_extension
ORDER BY avg_indent DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

### Commits by Weekday

``` sql
SELECT
    toDayOfWeek(time) AS weekday,
    count() AS commits,
    uniq(author) AS authors
FROM git.commits
GROUP BY weekday
ORDER BY weekday;
```

they describe the previous change of that line. To find the lines that
survived the longest:

``` sql
SELECT
    path,
    line_number_new,
    line,
    prev_author,
    prev_time,
    now() - prev_time AS age
FROM git.line_changes
WHERE (sign = 1) AND (line_type = 'Code')
ORDER BY prev_time ASC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Comments to Code Ratio by Author

``` sql
SELECT
    author,
    countIf(line_type = 'Comment') AS comments,
    countIf(line_type = 'Code') AS code,
    comments / code AS comments_to_code_ratio
FROM git.line_changes
WHERE sign = 1
GROUP BY author
HAVING code > 1000
ORDER BY comments_to_code_ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### Average Indentation by File Extension

The `indent` column contains the number of leading whitespaces of a line
(tabs are counted as 4 spaces), so you can compare coding styles:

``` sql
SELECT
    file_extension,
    avg(indent) AS avg_indent,
    quantile(0.9)(indent) AS p90_indent
FROM git.line_changes
WHERE (sign = 1) AND (line_type = 'Code')
GROUP BY file_extension
ORDER BY avg_indent DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

### Commits by Weekday

``` sql
SELECT
    toDayOfWeek(time) AS weekday,
    count() AS commits,
    uniq(author) AS authors
FROM git.commits
GROUP BY weekday
ORDER BY weekday;
```

sidebar_position: 38
sidebar_label: FUNCTION

# CREATE FUNCTION — user defined function (UDF)

Creates a user defined function from a lambda expression. The expression must consist of function parameters, constants, operators, or other function calls.

**Syntax**

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION name [ON CLUSTER cluster] AS (parameter0, ...) -> expression;
```

A function can have an arbitrary number of parameters.

There are a few restrictions:

- The name of a function must be unique among user defined and system functions.
- Recursive functions are not allowed.
- All variables used by a function must be specified in its parameter list.

If any restriction is violated then an exception is raised.

**Example**

Query:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION linear_equation AS (x, k, b) -> k * x + b;
SELECT number, linear_equation(number, 2, 1) FROM numbers(3);
```

Result:

```text
┌─number─┬─linear_equation(number, 2, 1)─┐
│      0 │                             1 │
│      1 │                             3 │

sidebar_label: DETACH
---

# DETACH Statement {#detach-statement}

Makes the server "forget" about the existence of a table or a materialized view. If the table or the materialized view is replicated, it will be removed from the cluster.

**Syntax**

```sql
DETACH TABLE|VIEW [IF EXISTS] [db.]name [ON CLUSTER cluster] [PERMANENTLY] [SYNC]
```

Detaching does not delete the data or metadata for the table or materialized view. If the server was not stopped, on the next launch the server will read the metadata and recall the table/view again. If the server was stopped, the table/view will not be re-attached automatically unless it was detached with `PERMANENTLY` modifier or the metadata file was deleted manually.

If a table or a materialized view was detached `PERMANENTLY`, it will not be reattached on the next server launch automatically, so it can be reattached only explicitly using [ATTACH](../../sql-reference/statements/attach.md) query. But the metadata of the table or materialized view is still kept on the server, and it can be re-attached with the `ATTACH` query.

`SYNC` modifier waits for the completion of the detaching process. Without the `SYNC` modifier the query returns immediately, while the table or materialized view may be detached asynchronously in the background.

**See Also**

-   [ATTACH statement](../../sql-reference/statements/attach.md)

sidebar_position: 45
sidebar_label: DROP
---

# DROP Statement {#drop-statement}

Deletes existing entity. If the `IF EXISTS` clause is specified, these queries do not return an error if the entity does not exist.

Most `DROP` queries support the `SYNC` modifier, which makes the query wait for the completion of the deletion. Without the `SYNC` modifier the query returns immediately, while the entity may be deleted asynchronously in the background.

## DROP DATABASE {#drop-database}

Deletes all tables inside the `db` database, and then deletes the `db` database itself.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP DATABASE [IF EXISTS] db [ON CLUSTER cluster] [SYNC]
```

## DROP TABLE {#drop-table}

Deletes one or more tables.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP [TEMPORARY] TABLE [IF EXISTS] [db1.]name_1 [ON CLUSTER cluster] [, [db2.]name_2 ...] [SYNC]
```

`SYNC` modifier waits for the completion of the dropping process: the query returns only after the table data and metadata are actually deleted (for replicated tables, after the deletion is propagated through replication).

:::note "Restriction"
    If the table was [detached](../../sql-reference/statements/detach.md) `PERMANENTLY`, it can not be dropped with the `DROP TABLE` query. To delete it, attach it again first.
:::

## DROP DICTIONARY {#drop-dictionary}

Deletes the dictionary.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP DICTIONARY [IF EXISTS] [db.]name [SYNC]
```

## DROP USER {#drop-user-statement}

Deletes a user.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP USER [IF EXISTS] name [,...] [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]
```

## DROP ROLE {#drop-role-statement}

Deletes a role. Deleted role is revoked from all the entities where it was assigned.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP ROLE [IF EXISTS] name [,...] [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]
```

## DROP ROW POLICY {#drop-row-policy-statement}

Deletes a row policy. Deleted row policy is revoked from all the entities where it was assigned.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP [ROW] POLICY [IF EXISTS] name [,...] ON [database.]table [,...] [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]
```

## DROP QUOTA {#drop-quota-statement}

Deletes a quota. Deleted quota is revoked from all the entities where it was assigned.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP QUOTA [IF EXISTS] name [,...] [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]
```

## DROP SETTINGS PROFILE {#drop-settings-profile-statement}

Deletes a settings profile. Deleted settings profile is revoked from all the entities where it was assigned.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP [SETTINGS] PROFILE [IF EXISTS] name [,...] [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]
```

## DROP VIEW {#drop-view}

Deletes a view. Views can be deleted by a `DROP TABLE` command as well but `DROP VIEW` checks that `[db.]name` is a view.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP VIEW [IF EXISTS] [db.]name [ON CLUSTER cluster] [SYNC]
```

## DROP FUNCTION {#drop-function}

Deletes a user defined function created by [CREATE FUNCTION](../../sql-reference/statements/create/function.md).
System functions can not be dropped.

**Syntax**

```sql
DROP FUNCTION [IF EXISTS] function_name
```

**Example**

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION linear_equation AS (x, k, b) -> k*x + b;
DROP FUNCTION linear_equation;
```

- the average time before code will be rewritten (the half-life of code decay);
- comments/code percentage change in time, by author, by location.

## The Dataset

The dataset describes a Git repository hosted on GitHub as three related
tables:

- `git.commits` — one row per commit: the hash, the author, the time, the
  commit message and per-commit statistics (files and lines added/deleted);
- `git.file_changes` — one row per file changed in a commit: the change type
  (add, delete, modify, rename), the path, and the statistics of the change;
- `git.line_changes` — the largest and most interesting table: one row per
  changed line, with the line content, its indentation and classification
  (empty, comment, punctuation, code), plus the commit, author and time of the
  previous change of this line — rough `git blame` information.

All three tables are ordered by time and can be joined by the commit hash, so
you can start with a high-level view in `git.commits` and drill down to
individual lines in `git.line_changes`. A quick sanity check after loading the
data:

``` sql
SELECT count() FROM git.commits;
SELECT uniq(author) FROM git.commits;
SELECT count() FROM git.line_changes WHERE sign = 1;
```

## Generating the Data

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys

def edit(path, old, new, count=1):
    with open(path) as f:
        content = f.read()
    n = content.count(old)
    assert n == count, f"{path}: expected {count} occurrence(s), found {n} for: {old[:80]!r}"
    content = content.replace(old, new)
    with open(path, 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)
    print(f"edited {path}")

payload.resultSummary:
All seven requirements implemented and committed. I identified the exact upstream PR for each slug via `requirements/.rename_map.json`, fetched the real diffs from GitHub to match the historical change precisely, and applied them to this older tree. Each commit was done under `flock /tmp/ch_git.lock`, staging only that requirement's files; shared files (`src/Core/Settings.h`, `MutateTask.cpp`) were edited inside the same locked section as their commit. All seven `requirement_patches/<slug>.diff` files are non-empty and unstaged.

- metrics-documentation-coverage: done — Settings.h description for `system_events_show_zero_values` now names `system.events` and `system.metrics` (all 92 metrics in CurrentMetrics.cpp already have ≥10-char docs, verified by script); added `02393_every_metric_must_have_documentation.{sql,reference}` (upstream PR #40645).
- minmax-idx2-files-to-skip: done — `collectFilesToSkip` in `src/Storages/MergeTree/MutateTask.cpp:448` now uses `index->getSerializedFileExtension()` instead of hardcoded `.idx` so MinMax `.idx2` files are skipped/rebuilt (PR #40095).
- minmaxany-read-size-check: done — in `AggregateFunctionMinMaxAny.h` `SingleValueDataString::read` casts capacity to Int32 and throws `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` when the rounded capacity overflows; `Arena::alloc` in `src/Common/Arena.h` now compares via `std::ptrdiff_t` to avoid pointer-overflow UB; added `02481_i43247_ubsan_in_minmaxany.{sql,reference}` (PR #43249).
- msan-getauxval-warning: done — upstream PR #43065 only added the `sanitizer/msan_interface.h` include (its base already had unpoison calls); this older `base/glibc-compatibility/musl/getauxval.c` predates that rewrite, so I added the include plus a guarded `__msan_unpoison` of the auxv pair before each read in `__find_auxv` — same intent, no behavior change.
- msgpack-uuid-column-check: done — `insertUUID` in `MsgPackRowInputFormat.cpp` now throws `ILLEGAL_COLUMN` when the target column isn't UUID-typed; added `02422_msgpack_uuid_wrong_column.{sql,reference}` (PR #41309).
- multipart-part-size-threshold: done — `s3_upload_part_size_multiply_parts_count_threshold` default 1000 → 500 in `src/Core/Settings.h:86` (PR #42392); diff verified to contain only that line.
- mutation-part-size-calculation: done — `finalizeMutatedPart` in MutateTask.cpp now sets bytes on disk from `checksums.getTotalSizeOnDisk()` instead of a filesystem walk, reordered with `default_codec`, plus stale-comment cleanup in `IMergeTreeDataPart::loadChecksums` (PR #39860).

Notes: the checkout has no `tests/queries/0_stateless/` directory (only `1_stateful`), so I created it for the new test files. No build was run (too slow); changes are faithful ports of the upstream fixes, with asserts confirming each edit applied exactly once.

# Оператор SELECT {#select-queries-syntax}

`SELECT` осуществляет выборку данных.

``` sql
SELECT [DISTINCT] expr_list
[FROM [db.]table | (subquery) | table_function]
[WHERE expr]
[LIMIT [n, ]m]
```

:::note "Примечание"
    Если запрос `SELECT` не содержит секцию `FROM`, то данные читаются из виртуальной таблицы `system.one`.
:::

Все секции, кроме списка выражений сразу после `SELECT`, являются необязательными.

:::danger "Предупреждение"
    Отсутствие секции `LIMIT` может привести к выборке очень большого объёма данных.
:::

Ниже секции запроса рассмотрены подробнее.

#!/bin/bash

# Resolves the id of a job of the current GitHub Actions workflow run by its name.
#
# The jobs API endpoint is paginated (30 entries per page by default), so for
# large workflows the target job may be located on a later page. Iterate over
# the pages, requesting the maximum page size, until the job is found. This
# keeps the number of API requests minimal and avoids spurious failures like
# "403 Client Error: rate limit exceeded for url".

GITHUB_JOB_ID() {
    local job_name="$1"
    local page=1

    while :; do
        local response
        response=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
            "https://api.github.com/repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100&page=$page")

        local job_id
        job_id=$(echo "$response" | jq -r --arg NAME "$job_name" '.jobs[] | select(.name == $NAME) | .id' | head -n1)
        if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
            echo "$job_id"
            return 0
        fi

        # A non-full page means there are no more jobs to scan.
        local jobs_on_page
        jobs_on_page=$(echo "$response" | jq '.jobs | length')
        if [ "$jobs_on_page" -lt 100 ]; then
            echo "Job '$job_name' not found in run $GITHUB_RUN_ID" >&2
            return 1
        fi

        page=$((page + 1))
    done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

CURDIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
# shellcheck source=../shell_config.sh
. "$CURDIR"/../shell_config.sh

# Regression for the memory accounting of two-level GROUP BY queries against
# max_memory_usage_for_user.
#
# The test had been flaky: the user memory tracker could drop to zero between
# the allocations of the main query, and the limit check did not trigger.
# A concurrent sleep(3) query keeps the user memory tracker active while the
# GROUP BY query is running, so the accounting contract is always covered.

$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q "SELECT sleep(3)" &

$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT --max_memory_usage_for_user=$((100 * 1024 * 1024)) -q "
    SELECT number FROM numbers_mt(100000000) GROUP BY number FORMAT Null
" 2>&1 | grep -c "MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"

wait

        # crc32 is optional in v8.0 and mandatory in v8.1. Enable it as __crc32()* is used in lot's of places and even very old ARM CPUs
        # support it.
        set (COMPILER_FLAGS "${COMPILER_FLAGS} -march=armv8+crc")
    else ()
        # ARMv8.2 is quite ancient but the lowest common denominator supported by both Graviton 2 and 3 processors [1]. In particular, it
        # includes LSE (made mandatory with ARMv8.1) which provides nice speedups without having to fall back to compat flag
        # "-moutline-atomics" for v8.0 [2, 3, 4] that requires a recent glibc with runtime dispatch helper, limiting our ability to run on
        # old OSs.
        #
        # simd:    NEON, introduced as optional in v8.0, A few extensions were added with v8.1 but it's still not mandatory. Enables the
        #          compiler to auto-vectorize.
        # sve:     Scalable Vector Extensions, introduced as optional in v8.2. Available in Graviton 3 but not in Graviton 2, and most likely
        #          also not in CI machines. Compiler support for autovectorization is rudimentary at the time of writing, see [5]. Can be
        #          enabled one-fine-day (TM) but not now.
        # ssbs:    "Speculative Store Bypass Safe". Optional in v8.0, mandatory in v8.5. Meltdown/spectre countermeasure.
        # crypto:  SHA1, SHA256, AES. Optional in v8.0. In v8.4, further algorithms were added but it's still optional, see [6].
        # dotprod: Scalar vector product (SDOT and UDOT instructions). Probably the most obscure extra flag with doubtful performance benefits
        #          but it has been activated since always, so why not enable it. It's not 100% clear in which revision this flag was
        #          introduced as optional, either in v8.2 [7] or in v8.4 [8].
        # ldapr:   Load-Acquire RCpc Register. Better support of release/acquire of atomics. Good for allocators and high contention code.
        #          Optional in v8.2, mandatory in v8.3 [9]. Supported in Graviton 2+, Azure and GCP instances. Generated from clang 15.
        #
        # [1] https://github.com/aws/aws-graviton-getting-started/blob/main/c-c%2B%2B.md
        # [2] https://community.arm.com/arm-community-blogs/b/tools-software-ides-blog/posts/making-the-most-of-the-arm-architecture-in-gcc-10
        # [3] https://mysqlonarm.github.io/ARM-LSE-and-MySQL/
        # [4] https://dev.to/aws-builders/large-system-extensions-for-aws-graviton-processors-3eci
        # [5] https://developer.arm.com/tools-and-software/open-source-software/developer-tools/llvm-toolchain/sve-support
        # [6] https://developer.arm.com/documentation/100067/0612/armclang-Command-line-Options/-mcpu?lang=en
        # [7] https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/ARM-Options.html
        # [8] https://developer.arm.com/documentation/102651/a/What-are-dot-product-intructions-
        # [9] https://developer.arm.com/documentation/dui0801/g/A64-Data-Transfer-Instructions/LDAPR?lang=en
        set (COMPILER_FLAGS "${COMPILER_FLAGS} -march=armv8.2-a+simd+crypto+dotprod+ssbs -Xclang=-target-feature -Xclang=+ldapr -Wno-unused-command-line-argument")

6	# DROP Statement {#drop-statement}
7	
8	Deletes existing entity. If the `IF EXISTS` clause is specified, these queries do not return an error if the entity does not exist.
9	
10	Most `DROP` queries support the `SYNC` modifier, which makes the query wait for the completion of the deletion. Without the `SYNC` modifier the query returns immediately, while the entity may be deleted asynchronously in the background.
11	
12	## DROP DATABASE {#drop-database}
13	
14	Deletes all tables inside the `db` database, and then deletes the `db` database itself.
15	
16	**Syntax**
17	
18	```sql
19	DROP DATABASE [IF EXISTS] db [ON CLUSTER cluster] [SYNC]
20	```
21	
22	## DROP TABLE {#drop-table}
23	
24	Deletes one or more tables.
25	
26	**Syntax**
27	
28	```sql
29	DROP [TEMPORARY] TABLE [IF EXISTS] [db1.]name_1 [ON CLUSTER cluster] [, [db2.]name_2 ...] [SYNC]
30	```
31	
32	`SYNC` modifier waits for the completion of the dropping process: the query returns only after the table data and metadata are actually deleted (for replicated tables, after the deletion is propagated through replication).
33	
34	:::note "Restriction"
35	    If the table was [detached](../../sql-reference/statements/detach.md) `PERMANENTLY`, it can not be dropped with the `DROP TABLE` query. To delete it, attach it again first.
36	:::
37	
38	## DROP DICTIONARY {#drop-dictionary}
39	
40	Deletes the dictionary.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Lambda handler rotating the GitHub Actions self-hosted runner token.

The lambda is deployed as a plain zip package (see template.yaml). It fetches
the GitHub credentials from AWS Secrets Manager, requests a fresh runner
registration token from the GitHub API and stores it back to the secret, so
that new CI runners can always register with a valid token.
"""

import json
import os
import urllib.request

import boto3

SECRET_NAME = os.environ["SECRET_NAME"]
GITHUB_ORG = os.environ.get("GITHUB_ORG", "ClickHouse")

secrets_client = boto3.client("secretsmanager")


def github_request(url: str, token: str, method: str = "GET") -> dict:
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, method=method)
    request.add_header("Accept", "application/vnd.github.v3+json")
    request.add_header("Authorization", f"token {token}")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
        return json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))


def rotate_runner_token() -> None:
    secret = json.loads(
        secrets_client.get_secret_value(SecretId=SECRET_NAME)["SecretString"]
    )

    response = github_request(
        f"https://api.github.com/orgs/{GITHUB_ORG}/actions/runners/registration-token",
        secret["github_token"],
        method="POST",
    )

    secret["runner_token"] = response["token"]
    secrets_client.put_secret_value(
        SecretId=SECRET_NAME, SecretString=json.dumps(secret)
    )


def lambda_handler(event, context):
    rotate_runner_token()
    return {"statusCode": 200, "body": "runner token rotated"}

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Description: Rotates the GitHub Actions runner registration token on a schedule.

Globals:
  Function:
    Timeout: 60
    MemorySize: 128

Resources:
  RunnerTokenRotationLambda:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: runner_token_rotation_lambda
      PackageType: Zip
      Runtime: python3.9
      Handler: app.lambda_handler
      CodeUri: .
      Environment:
        Variables:
          SECRET_NAME: !Ref RunnerTokenSecretName
          GITHUB_ORG: ClickHouse
      Policies:
        - AWSSecretsManagerReadWritePolicy: {}
      Events:
        RotationSchedule:
          Type: Schedule
          Properties:
            Schedule: rate(1 hour)
            Description: Periodically refresh the runner registration token.

Parameters:
  RunnerTokenSecretName:
    Type: String
    Description: Name of the AWS Secrets Manager secret holding the GitHub and runner tokens.

Outputs:
  RunnerTokenRotationLambdaArn:
    Description: ARN of the deployed lambda.
    Value: !GetAtt RunnerTokenRotationLambda.Arn

#!/bin/bash
# Builds the lambda zip artifact and deploys it via SAM.
# The lambda is packaged as a zip archive (PackageType: Zip), no container
# image is involved.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"

LAMBDA_NAME=runner_token_rotation_lambda
ZIP_PACKAGE="${LAMBDA_NAME}.zip"

rm -f "${ZIP_PACKAGE}"
zip -9 "${ZIP_PACKAGE}" app.py

sam build --template template.yaml
sam deploy \
    --no-confirm-changeset \
    --stack-name "${LAMBDA_NAME}" \
    --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM \
    --resolve-s3

rm -f "${ZIP_PACKAGE}"

# CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE Statement {#create-settings-profile-statement}

Creates a [settings profile](../../operations/access-rights.md#settings-profiles-management) that can be assigned to a user or a role.

**Syntax**

```sql
CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE [IF NOT EXISTS | OR REPLACE] name [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]
    [SETTINGS variable [= value] [MIN [=] min_value] [MAX [=] max_value] [READONLY | WRITABLE] | INHERIT 'profile_name'] [,...]
```

Note that there is no separate `SETTING CONSTRAINTS` clause: constraints on a setting are specified inline, right after the setting name and its value, using the `MIN`, `MAX`, `READONLY` and `WRITABLE` keywords.

**Example**

```sql
CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE max_memory_usage_profile
SETTINGS max_memory_usage = 100000001 MIN 90000000 MAX 110000000
TO robin
```

## ALTER SETTINGS PROFILE Statement {#alter-settings-profile-statement}

Modifies a settings profile.

**Syntax**

```sql
ALTER SETTINGS PROFILE [IF EXISTS] name [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]
    [RENAME TO new_name]
    [SETTINGS variable [= value] [MIN [=] min_value] [MAX [=] max_value] [READONLY | WRITABLE] | INHERIT 'profile_name'] [,...]
```

 ## Zero-copy Replication (not ready for production) {#zero-copy}
 
-ClickHouse supports zero-copy replication for `S3` and `HDFS` disks, which means that if the data is stored remotely on several machines and needs to be synchronized, then only the metadata is replicated (paths to the data parts), but not the data itself.
+Zero-copy replication is possible, but not recommended, with  `S3` and `HDFS` disks. Zero-copy replication means that if the data is stored remotely on several machines and needs to be synchronized, then only the metadata is replicated (paths to the data parts), but not the data itself.
+
+:::warning Zero-copy replication is not ready for production
+Zero-copy replication is disabled by default in ClickHouse version 22.8 and higher.  This feature is not recommended for production use.
+:::

  (both `HAVING` fused into the aggregation and a `WHERE` in an outer

  outer `LIMIT`. The optimization must not push the limit past the
  filter; the test asserts the result is identical with

import time


def check_replication_consistency(nodes, table, timeout=300):
    """Check that all given replicas of `table` are consistent.

    Waits until every node has processed its replication queue, polling at
    one-second intervals for at most `timeout` seconds, and then runs
    SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA on each node. Both phases share one time budget:
    the sync step receives only the part of the original `timeout` that
    remains after the polling loop, instead of a full extra timeout.
    """
    started = time.time()

    for node in nodes:
        for _ in range(timeout):
            queue_size = int(node.query("SELECT count() FROM system.replication_queue").strip())
            if queue_size == 0:
                break
            time.sleep(1)

    elapsed = time.time() - started
    remaining_timeout = max(timeout - elapsed, 1)

    for node in nodes:
        node.query(
            f"SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA {table}",
            settings={"receive_timeout": remaining_timeout},
        )

Note: the workspace was missing `src/Common/SharedLibrary.h` from the start, so the header had to be recreated. Dynamic loading (dlopen/dlsym/dlclose) is now confined to library-bridge; the main `clickhouse` binary no longer compiles it via `src/Common`.
- `remove-grouping-sets-parser`: done — removed the dead `WITH GROUPING SETS` modifier branch in `src/Parsers/ParserSelectQuery.cpp` (it set `group_by_with_grouping_sets` without ever parsing a grouping-sets list; no tests referenced it). The supported `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS (...)` syntax is untouched.
- `remove-legacy-cache-dirs`: done — removed the `data_cache_path`-based `FILESYSTEM_CACHE_PATHS` readarray and its entry in the mkdir/chown loop in `docker/server/entrypoint.sh`; `bash -n` passes.
- `remove-libexecinfo-leftovers`: done — removed the dangling `${EXECINFO_LIBRARIES}` references (defined nowhere) from `src/CMakeLists.txt` and `src/Daemon/CMakeLists.txt`; edit+commit done inside one flock section since `src/CMakeLists.txt` is a shared file.
- `remove-localhost-replica-test`: done with caveat — the historical change (upstream PR #39862) deletes `SET prefer_localhost_replica=0;` from `tests/queries/0_stateless/02352_grouby_shadows_arg.sql`, but that test does not exist in this older snapshot (verified: no `prefer_localhost_replica` anywhere under `tests/`). Best-faith change: created `02352_grouby_shadows_arg.sql` and its `.reference` in the exact post-PR upstream state (fetched from the upstream merge commit), i.e. the test reflecting current defaults without the obsolete setting.
- `remove-obsolete-clion-comments`: done — removed the stale "CLion does not support Ninja" comment block and the `CLION_IDE` exception from the Ninja generator check in `PreLoad.cmake`, keeping the Xcode special-casing (matches upstream PR #40653 exactly).

payload.resultSummary:
All seven requirements are implemented and committed. Each change was modeled on the actual historical ClickHouse commit (verified against upstream patches via GitHub API), adapted to this older workspace state.

Per-slug report:

- `llvm-build-config`: done — added `set (LLVM_ENABLE_ZSTD 0 CACHE INTERNAL "")` alongside the other disabled LLVM toggles in `contrib/llvm-cmake/CMakeLists.txt` (upstream commit dbed82e).
- `llvm-integration-cleanups`: done — `contrib/llvm-cmake/CMakeLists.txt`: removed the stale commented-out `llvm_libs_all` function block and the obsolete `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17` override (with its comment), and documented that LLVM is still built statically under `USE_STATIC_LIBRARIES=0`. The `15.0.0bundled` version bump itself had just been committed by a concurrent agent (`jit-llvm-15-migration`); my diff keeps that baseline and covers the remaining cleanups (upstream commit c08387e).
- `llvm-sanitizer-workaround`: done — `cmake/sanitize.cmake:19` switched ASan flags from `-fsanitize-address-use-after-scope` to `-fno-sanitize-address-use-after-scope` with a comment citing llvm/llvm-project#58633 (upstream commit f5270a6), byte-identical to upstream.
- `llvm-symbolizer-symlink`: done — `docker/packager/binary/Dockerfile`: added `RUN ln -s /usr/bin/llvm-symbolizer-${LLVM_VERSION} /usr/bin/llvm-symbolizer` (comment `# for external_symbolizer_path`) before `COPY build.sh /`. Adapted from the upstream hardcoded `llvm-symbolizer-15` to the image's `LLVM_VERSION=14` variable, matching the existing `ld.lld` symlink idiom (upstream commit 64f9571).
- `load-balancing-priority-lifetime`: done — `src/Common/GetPriorityForLoadBalancing.cpp`: changed `[&]` captures to `[this]` and `[this, pool_size]` in `getPriorityFunc()` so the returned `std::function` no longer references stack data (upstream commit 8c5583d; resulting blob hash identical to upstream).
- `log-engine-incremental-backups`: done — applied upstream commit 007ae0e's C++ fixes: `HashingReadBuffer.h` now hashes incrementally via a `hashing_begin` cursor with a `getHash()` override; `ConcatSeekableReadBuffer::BufferInfo` got a nulling move constructor (`std::exchange`); `PartMetadataManagerWithCache.cpp` calls `hbuf.ignoreAll()` before `getHash()`. All four post-change blob hashes match upstream exactly. Two upstream hunks were not applicable to this older checkout: `BackupImpl.cpp`'s `checkBaseBackupForFile` doesn't exist here (the equivalent inline logic already guards `size >= base_size`, so the inverted-comparison bug is absent), and `tests/integration/` is trimmed from this workspace, so the new integration test could not be added.
- `logging-ignore-memory-limits`: done — `src/Loggers/OwnSplitChannel.cpp`: hoisted `LockMemoryExceptionInThread lock_memory_tracker(VariableContext::Global)` to the top of `tryLogSplit()` so the whole logging path (not just the exception handler) ignores memory limits (upstream commit 3137476).

All commits were made under `/tmp/ch_git.lock` with explicit file staging only; all seven `requirement_patches/*.diff` files are non-empty (verified with `wc -c`, 463–2911 bytes each). Other agents' working-tree changes were left untouched.

- `unhex-fixedstring-support`: done — `DecodeFromBinaryRepresentation` in `src/Functions/FunctionsBinaryRepresentation.cpp` now accepts `FixedString` (`isStringOrFixedString` type check + a `ColumnFixedString` execution branch decoding `n`-sized rows with the same semantics as `String`).
- `uninline-error-handling`: done — moved `dateIsNotSupported` / `dateTimeIsNotSupported` out of `src/Functions/DateTimeTransforms.h` (now declarations) into new `src/Functions/DateTimeTransforms.cpp`; identical `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` throws preserved. The Functions CMake target globs sources, so no build-file change needed.
- `uniq-injective-elimination`: done, with caveat — this snapshot has no `src/Analyzer` tree (pre-analyzer checkout), so the pass cannot be wired into a pass manager. Best-faith: added `src/Analyzer/Passes/UniqInjectiveFunctionsEliminationPass.{h,cpp}` implementing the historical pass (removes single-argument injective ordinary functions inside `uniq`/`uniqExact`/`uniqHLL12`/`uniqTheta`/`uniqCombined`/`uniqCombined64` via `InDepthQueryTreeVisitor` + `FunctionFactory::isInjective`). The old-pipeline equivalent already exists via `RemoveInjectiveFunctionsVisitor`.
- `unique-query-thread-ids`: done — `thread_ids` changed from `std::vector<UInt64>` to `std::unordered_set<UInt64>` in `src/Common/ThreadStatus.h`, `src/Interpreters/ProcessList.h` (plus `<unordered_set>` include), and `src/Interpreters/QueryLog.h`; `src/Interpreters/ThreadStatusExt.cpp:120` now uses `insert` instead of `emplace_back`. Verified all consumers (`QueryLog.cpp`, `executeQuery.cpp`, `ProcessList.cpp`) only copy/iterate, so set semantics are compatible.
- `unused-constructor-removal`: done — removed the unused (and incorrect, non-cumulative) `MergeTreeIndexGranularity(size_t marks_count, size_t fixed_granularity)` constructor from `src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexGranularity.h/.cpp`; repo-wide grep confirmed zero call sites (superseded by `resizeWithFixedGranularity`).

Verification: no full build (too slow, per instructions); correctness checks were grep-based — confirmed zero call sites for the removed constructor, all `thread_ids` consumers compatible with `unordered_set`, and `isStringOrFixedString` availability.
